items.title: Association between Multimorbidity and Suicidal Behaviors among People with Psychotic Disorders.
items.authors: Saito A, Piché F, Kavalidou K, Baillot A, Juster RP, Consortium S, Romain AJ.

sections.heading: Background and hypothesis
sections.text: Suicide and poor health conditions are the leading causes of premature mortality in psychotic disorders. People with psychotic disorders have an increased risk of multimorbidity (≥2 chronic conditions) which could contribute to higher rates of suicidal ideation and suicide behaviors. The aim of the present study was to determine the association between multimorbidity and suicidal behaviors in people with psychotic disorders.

sections.heading: Study design
sections.text: Cross-sectional study using data from the Signature Biobank and including people with clinical diagnoses of psychotic disorders. Sociodemographic information, lifestyle habits, 22 chronic conditions, suicidal ideation (PHQ-9), and suicidal behaviors (SBQ-R) scores were gathered. Logistic regressions were performed across three models with different levels of adjustment: sociodemographics (M1), M1 adjusted for psychotic symptoms (M2), and M2 with further adjustments for lifestyle habits (M3). Sensitivity analyses were done on a subgroup of individuals with early psychosis (≤30 years old).

sections.heading: Study results
sections.text: A sample of 748 participants with diagnosis of psychotic disorder (69% male; age: 39.5 ± 14.1; 35.2% with schizophrenia was recruited. Among them, 407 participants (54%) had multimorbidity, and 44% had physical multimorbidity. After adjustment for covariates, individuals with multimorbidity were more likely to report suicidal ideations (OR 2.31, 95%CI [1.61-3.32]) and suicidal behaviors (OR 1.84, 95%CI [1.15-2.97]) than their counterparts. Similar results were found for the young psychosis subgroup (<30 years old), as for physical multimorbidity.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Results confirmed an association between multimorbidity and higher rates of suicidal behaviors among our sample, supporting the importance of interventions to prevent the development of chronic conditions.

items.title: Extra-Synaptic Functions of NRG1 Type I Signaling in Hippocampal γ-Oscillations.
items.authors: Soto-Bernardini MC, Jeong S, Hosseinnia H, Altas B, Rhee HJ, Lee C, Schill Y, Zeitschel U, Götze T, Hellriegel J, Lehning M, Brenes O, Fornaguera J, Mora-Villalobos JA, Fledrich R, Stassart RM, Rhee JS, Schwab MH.

sections.heading: Background and hypothesis
sections.text: The neurodevelopmental hypothesis of schizophrenia posits that early-acting genetic risk factors precipitate pathological neurodevelopmental processes that result in neural network dysfunctions during adolescence. Human gene variants of the epidermal growth factor-like ligand Neuregulin 1 (NRG1) and its tyrosine kinase receptor ErbB4 are putative risk factors in schizophrenia, and aberrant NRG1 signaling has been implicated in schizophrenia-relevant endophenotypes. However, insight into associated pathomechanisms remains limited.

sections.heading: Study design
sections.text: We modeled embryonic glutamatergic neuron-specific NRG1 type I overexpression in a conditional transgenic mouse line to investigate the impact of early hyperactive NRG1 type I signaling on neuronal network functions in the hippocampus in vivo.

sections.heading: Study results
sections.text: NRG1 type I transgenic mice display abnormal gamma-frequency network oscillations in the adolescent hippocampus, in the absence of neuroinflammation or changes in hippocampal morphology. Instead, we found extra-synaptic NRG1 type I accumulation, which was associated with ErbB4 hyperphosphorylation, an increased size and number of Kv2.1 potassium channel-marked endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-plasma membrane (PM) junctions, and a reduction of A-type potassium channel currents in pyramidal cells.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Together, these findings suggest a model in which early-onset extra-synaptic NRG1 type I accumulation at ER-PM junctions causes sustained changes in neuronal excitability, ultimately contributing to deficits in neuronal network oscillations as observed in various neuropsychiatric disorders.

items.title: DYSBIOSIS OF GUT MICROBIOTA IN PATIENTS HOSPITALIZED FOR THE TREATMENT OF ALCOHOL USE DISORDER.
items.authors: Thoen RU, Longo L, Basso BS, Rampelotto PH, Sordi AO, Kessler FHP, Diemen LV, Álvares-DA-Silva MR.

sections.heading: Background and objectives
sections.text: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) is a global issue with a significant financial impact on health. The main objective of this study was to assess the chronic effect of alcohol on the composition and diversity of intestinal microbiota in AUD patients.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Prospective cohort study in patients hospitalized for AUD treatment. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data and inflammatory markers were assessed at the time of hospital admission for AUD-T1-group and in the control group, as well evaluation of the gut microbiota composition, while the AUD-T2-group was assessed at the discharge from hospital treatment.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: 50 participants were included in the control group and 47 admitted for AUD treatment. The mean age in the AUD-T1-group was 49.3 years, all male. Mieloperoxidase concentration was significantly higher in AUD-T1-group compared to control (P<0.001). The opposite was observed for E-selectin (P<0.001). Global alpha diversity was different among the control, AUD-T1 and AUD-T2 groups, ACE index (P<0.004), Shannon index (P<0.017), observed taxa (P=0.002). The LEfSe algorithm identified a higher abundance of Faecalibacterium, Bacteroides, Agathobacter, and Ruminococcaceae unclassified in control compared to the AUD-T1. There were no differences in the abundance of bacterial genera between the AUD-T1 and AUD-T2 groups.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Patients with AUD exhibit changes in intestinal microbiota composition, potentially associated with low-grade inflammation and functional alterations that contribute to the development of diseases. The composition of intestinal microbiota and its bioactive metabolites may serve as novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of AUD.

items.title: Nomogram for predicting the response of modified electroconvulsive therapy in patients with bipolar depressive episodes: a retrospective cohort study.
items.authors: Wang Y, Wang Z, Bai H, Liu M, Li W, Yu S, Tang X, Tang X.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Depressive episodes are a major manifestation of bipolar disorder, a common mental illness associated with substantial morbidity and premature mortality. Modified electroconvulsive therapy (MECT) is an effective physical treatment for bipolar depressive episodes. However, the clinical response to MECT varies considerably among individuals, and effective predictive indicators are still lacking. This study aimed to develop a nomogram prediction model for MECT response in patients with bipolar depressive episodes.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective set study enrolled 318 patients with bipolar depressive episodes who were randomly divided into a training set (n = 222) and a validation set (n = 96) at a 7:3 ratio. Based on the MECT response, the 222 patients in the training set were classified into responders (n = 175) and non-responders (n = 47). All patients were assessed using the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17), response was defined as a reduction of at least 50% in the total HAMD-17 score. Sociodemographic, clinical, electrocardiogram, and echocardiogram parameters were collected. Independent predictors were identified using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses, and a nomogram prediction model was constructed. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration was assessed using calibration curves, and clinical applicability was evaluated using decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation was performed using the Bootstrap method.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among the training set, 175 patients (78.8%) were responders and 47 (21.2%) non-responders. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that higher educational level, longer P wave duration, and higher standard deviation of normal NN intervals (SDNN) were independent protective factors for MECT response, whereas increased left atrial diameter was an independent risk factor. The nomogram incorporating these four predictors achieved AUCs of 0.872 in the training set and 0.893 in the validation set. Calibration curves indicated good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. DCA demonstrated a significant net benefit of the model.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The nomogram model, incorporating educational level, P wave duration, SDNN, and left atrial diameter, demonstrated favorable predictive performance and clinical utility for MECT response in bipolar depressive episodes. This model provides clinicians with an objective basis to early identify patients likely to benefit and optimize individualized therapies.

items.title: Prevalence and associated factors of suicidal ideation, suicide plans, and suicide attempts among nurses: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Huang W, Wan B, Yang C, Hu J, Jia Q.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Suicide-related outcomes among nurses represent an important occupational mental health concern; however, evidence regarding their prevalence and associated factors remains fragmented. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of suicidal ideation (SI) and suicide plans (SP) among nurses, narratively summarize suicide attempts (SA), and synthesize associated factors.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, PsycINFO, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and four Chinese databases (CNKI, CBM, VIP, and Wanfang) from inception to November 1, 2025. Random-effects models were used to estimate pooled prevalence, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and 95% prediction intervals (PIs) for SI and SP. Subgroup analyses and meta-regression were conducted to explore heterogeneity. Publication bias for SI was assessed using a funnel plot and Egger's test. Associated factors were synthesized narratively, and SA-related findings were summarized narratively because of limited available data and substantial heterogeneity.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 1,840 records were initially identified, and 55 articles representing 54 independent studies across 18 countries were included. The pooled prevalence was 12.8% (95% CI: 10.1%-15.7%; 95% PI: 3.2%-36.3%; I² = 99.0%) for SI and 5.0% (95% CI: 3.8%-6.4%; 95% PI: 1.6%-17.6%; I² = 70.2%) for SP, indicating substantial heterogeneity for SI and moderate-to-high heterogeneity for SP. In subgroup analyses, SI prevalence varied by country, geographical region, and recall period. By country, SI prevalence ranged from 6.1% in Spain to 15.5% in Ireland. Regionally, Asia showed the highest SI prevalence (15.7%), followed by Europe (10.8%) and North America (8.6%). Across recall periods, SI prevalence was highest for past-week recall (18.1%) and lowest for past-month recall (8.1%). Meta-regression indicated a negative association between mean age and SI prevalence (R² = 25.86%). SA was reported in a limited number of studies and was summarized narratively because of heterogeneity in measurement and populations. Associated factors spanned multiple domains, with psychological and occupational factors most frequently reported.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: SI and SP are relatively common among nurses, whereas evidence on SA remains limited. The wide prediction intervals suggest that pooled prevalence estimates should be interpreted as summary measures of heterogeneous evidence rather than precise estimates applicable to all nurse populations. Suicide-related outcomes among nurses appear to be influenced by individual psychological factors as well as occupational and contextual conditions, highlighting the need for targeted mental health support and workplace-based preventive strategies.

items.title: [Factors associated with transitions in the status of intimate partner violence in older adults: the EpiFloripa Idoso longitudinal study].
items.authors: Conceição TB, Warmling D, Araujo PG, Lindner SR.

sections.text: This study aimed to investigate the association between previous exposure to violence, depressive symptoms, and alcohol use and changes in intimate partner violence status in older adults in EpiFloripa Idoso. This longitudinal study analyzed cohort data by multinomial logistic regression. It categorized intimate partner violence according to violence (perpetration and victimization) status change over time. Its final sample consisted of 336 participants (those who answered the instrument in both time measurements). The following factors were associated with the onset of the perpetration: depressive symptoms with a history of violence (OR = 4.93; 95%CI: 1.10-21.30) and high alcohol consumption (OR = 2.77; 95%CI: 1.12-6.84). Perpetration continuity was associated with depressive symptoms with (OR = 8.09; 95%CI: 2.34-27.97) and without (OR = 4.44; 95%CI: 1.18-16.60) history of violence. The onset of victimization was associated with depressive symptoms with a history of violence (OR = 9.40; 95%CI: 1.94-45.47). Victimization continuity was associated with depressive symptoms with (OR = 10.20; 95%CI: 2.48-41.94) and without history of violence (OR = 8.04; 95%CI: 1.91-33.81). This study finds the need for integrated actions in mental health and in coping with violence in children and older adults as they can help to prevent future intimate partner violence. Limitations include self-reported measures, potential recall bias, limitations of the instrument for older adults, and analytical restrictions due to the sample size.

items.title: Cognitive Trajectories over 13 Years in Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorders: Addressing Selective Dropout Bias.
items.authors: Lee M, Matheson GJ, Lee EE, Holmqvist S, Nyman H, Agartz I, Hwong AR, Jönsson EG.

sections.heading: Background and hypothesis
sections.text: The longitudinal course of cognitive functioning in schizophrenia is debated. Previous longitudinal studies have reported selective attrition. We aimed to analyze cognitive trajectories over 13 years among patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSDs) in comparison with controls, while accounting for dropout bias, and explored baseline predictors of cognitive outcome.

sections.heading: Study design
sections.text: Cognition was assessed at study start, 5-year, and 13-year follow-up in 108 participants with schizophrenia spectrum disorder and 85 controls of similar age. Linear Mixed Effects models were used to model trajectories over time, with inverse probability weights to account for non-random dropout in patients. Predictors of cognitive function at 13 years were explored using linear regression.

sections.heading: Study results
sections.text: Retention was 51% for patients and 65% for controls. At study start, patients who dropped out performed worse on most cognitive tasks and were significantly older (4.5 years) than completers. In primary inverse probability of attrition weight-weighted analyses, patients scored lower than controls across nearly all cognitive domains (cognitive composite: β = -0.91 SD [95% CI -1.42, -0.39]) but their trajectories did not significantly differ from those of controls. Higher age predicted worse cognitive function. Illness duration was an independent negative predictor in patients. Study start cognition predicted 13-year follow-up cognition in patients.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Although cognitive performance of patients was lower than that of controls at study start, their change in performance over 13 years did not differ from the controls. Patients who dropped out were more cognitively impaired, highlighting risk of attrition bias. The robustness of findings across weighted and unweighted analyses strengthens confidence in the observed trajectories.

items.title: Cancer risk among individuals with mental illness - a systematic review and meta-analysis of nordic register-based prospective studies.
items.authors: Xiao X, Sadeghi F, Murphy G, Zhang Z, Andreassen OA, Valdimarsdóttir U, Fang F, Barker MM.

sections.text: Although cancer patients have a high burden of mental illness, it is less clear whether patients with mental illness experience a higher-than-expected cancer risk. This systematic review investigated the associations between a wide range of types of mental illness and subsequent cancer risk. Five electronic databases were searched for articles published from database initiation to October 24, 2024. Studies using nationwide Nordic register data to conduct a prospective analysis of the association between mental illness diagnosis and cancer incidence were included. When data from three or more countries were available for a given type of mental illness, random effects meta-analyses were performed; otherwise, narrative syntheses were conducted. A total of 7,767 non-duplicate articles were screened, of which 20 were included. Meta-analyses showed no association between schizophrenia diagnosis and overall cancer risk; however, a high level of heterogeneity was detected between studies. Individuals with schizophrenia appeared to have a higher risk of breast cancer (pooled standardized incidence ratio [SIR]: 1.28, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.08-1.52), and lower risks of rectal cancer (pooled SIR: 0.75, 95% CI: 0.59-0.95) and prostate cancer (pooled SIR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.48-0.59), compared to individuals in the general population. A higher risk of overall cancer was observed for mood, anxiety, and stress-related disorders, as well as autism and intellectual disability, in multiple studies; however, the results differed by cancer types and sex. In summary, these findings suggest an altered risk of cancer among individuals with mental illness living in Nordic countries. Further research is needed to enable the development of targeted cancer prevention strategies to reduce mental health disparities in cancer protection.

items.title: Hippocampal subregion volume alterations at baseline and following antidepressant treatment in youth at high risk for bipolar disorder.
items.authors: Tang B, Patino LR, Blom TJ, Welge JA, Strawn JR, Bruns KM, Zhang W, Lui S, Singh MK, DelBello MP.

sections.text: Understanding hippocampal neurostructural alterations at baseline and following antidepressant treatment in high-risk youth, particularly within distinct subregions, is critical for elucidating bipolar disorder (BD) pathophysiology and treatment planning. In this prospective randomized clinical trial, 105 high-risk youth with a first-degree BD-I relative(s) and moderate to severe depression and/or anxiety disorder, along with 51 healthy controls (HCs), were recruited. All participants underwent baseline structural MRI and clinical evaluations for depression, anxiety, and adverse events. High-risk youth were then randomized to receive psychotherapy and with either escitalopram or placebo. After 4 weeks of treatment, high-risk youth underwent repeated structural MRI and clinical assessments. These clinical assessments continued biweekly over the remaining 12 weeks of treatment (up to week 16). Volumetric measurements of hippocampal subregions were analyzed at baseline and 4 weeks. Compared to HCs, high-risk youth had significant baseline volume increases in the right cornu ammonis (CA)3, bilateral CA4, bilateral granule cell and molecular layers of the dentate gyrus (GC-ML-DG), and bilateral molecular layer, but reduced volumes in the bilateral fimbria and left parasubiculum. Volume reduction in the left hippocampal tail after 4 weeks of escitalopram treatment was associated with improvements in disinhibition and impulsivity symptoms from baseline to 4 weeks, and this association remained significant from baseline to 16 weeks. CA3-4 and GC-ML-DG enlargement may reflect adaptive changes, while fimbria and parasubiculum atrophy indicate vulnerabilities in BD-risk youth. Escitalopram-related volume reduction in the left hippocampal tail may reflect neural plasticity associated with emotional symptom improvement in BD high-risk youth. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: Mechanism of Antidepressant-Related Dysfunctional Arousal in High-Risk Youth; https://clinicaltrials.gov/; NCT02553161.

items.title: Temporal elements of speech in mania.
items.authors: Joyce JB, Ayala IN, Mishra S, Chatzisofroniou G, Clemens E, Yu H, Kendall T, Attia Z, Lin B, Frye MA.

sections.text: Computational analysis of speech enables precise, objective measurements of a behavioral signal closely linked to manic episodes. In a prospective cohort study conducted in Rochester, MN (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05956340), eighteen English-speaking adults voluntarily hospitalized for a manic episode of Bipolar I Disorder between August 2023 and September 2024 were enrolled. Participants completed semi-structured research interviews during both acute episodes and remission, with manic symptom severity assessed at each session using the Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS). Across 57 recorded interviews, temporal prosodic features were extracted using a novel end-to-end computational pipeline. After adjusting for individual differences and moderating effects, participant articulation rate (β = 0.24, p = 0.0038), speech rate variability (β = 0.23, p = 0.0041), floor transfer offset (β = -0.31, p = 0.007), and speaking duration (β = 0.54, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with manic symptom severity. These exploratory findings were largely independent of medication effects, as well as the presence of psychotic or mixed symptoms. These temporal elements classified manic (CV AUC = 0.85) and remission (CV AUC = 0.83) status, highlighting their potential as monitoring biomarkers for manic episodes.

items.title: CHARACTERIZATION OF PATIENTS TREATED AT A UNIVERSITY OUTPATIENT CLINIC WITH FUNCTIONAL DYSPEPSIA AND ITS CORRELATION WITH MENTAL DISORDERS.
items.authors: Korman DRE, Honorato JC, Melo JBT, Santos LLKD.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Functional dyspepsia is a common gastrointestinal disorder in clinical practice, characterized by chronic dyspeptic symptoms in the absence of identifiable organic disease, and is currently classified as a disorder of gut-brain interaction. Evidence suggests a significant association between functional dyspepsia and mental disorders, particularly anxiety and depression; however, this relationship remains insufficiently explored in national studies.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To characterize the sociodemographic and clinical profile of patients treated at a university outpatient gastrointestinal care clinic with functional dyspepsia and to analyze its correlation with mental disorders.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This was a cross-sectional observational study based on the analysis of medical records of patients diagnosed with functional dyspepsia according to the Rome IV criteria, treated at a university outpatient clinic in the southeast of Brazil. Sociodemographic data, lifestyle habits, clinical comorbidities, presence of concomitant mental disorders, and information on clinical evolution were collected. Statistical analyses were performed to evaluate associations between functional dyspepsia, mental disorders and clinical variables.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The sample consisted of 135 patients, predominantly women, with a higher prevalence of patients over 60 years of age. Most individuals were sedentary, non-smokers, and non-alcohol users, with systemic arterial hypertension being the most frequent clinical comorbidity. Mental disorders were present in nearly half of the patients, with generalized anxiety disorder and major depressive disorder being the most prevalent diagnoses, either isolated or in combination. No statistically significant associations were observed between mental disorders and most sociodemographic or clinical variables, except for obesity. During outpatient follow-up, a substantial proportion of patients with functional dyspepsia and concomitant mental disorders showed partial or complete improvement of dyspeptic symptoms.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The findings demonstrate a high frequency of mental disorders among patients with functional dyspepsia treated at a university outpatient clinic, reinforcing the multifactorial nature of this condition. The observed association and the clinical improvement identified in a subset of patients undergoing multidisciplinary follow-up highlight the importance of integrating gastroenterology and mental health care in the management of functional dyspepsia, contributing to a more comprehensive and interdisciplinary care of the patient.

items.title: Associations between adverse childhood experiences, depression, and empathy among Thai medical students: implications for trauma-informed medical education.
items.authors: Jongbowonwiwat K, Woonkaew W, Pitanupong T, Saelim N, Pitanupong J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) can influence emotional development and long-term mental health. Empathy, a core professional competency in medical education, may be shaped not only by training but also by early life adversity and current psychological distress. However, evidence specifically examining the association between ACEs and empathy among medical students in Southeast Asia remains limited. This study aimed to examine the association between ACEs and empathy among Thai medical students. We also examined whether depressive symptoms were independently related to empathy after adjusting for ACE exposure and other covariates.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted between April and July 2025 among first- to sixth-year medical students at a Faculty of Medicine and two affiliated medical education centers in Southern Thailand. A total of 540 students (response rate 77.1%) completed anonymous self-administered questionnaires, including demographic characteristics, the Thai ACE questionnaire, the Toronto Empathy Questionnaire (TEQ), and the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Empathy was analyzed as a continuous outcome using multiple linear regression, with logistic regression using TEQ < 45 as the cutoff performed as a sensitivity analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among 540 participants, 54.4% reported at least one ACE. The mean TEQ score was 45.6 (SD = 6.6). In multivariable linear regression, exposure to 1-2 ACEs (β = -1.75, p = 0.003) and depressive symptoms (β = -0.33, p < 0.001) were independently associated with lower empathy scores. In contrast, current life stress showed a modest but statistically significant positive association with empathy (β = 1.47, p = 0.024). Sensitivity analyses using logistic regression yielded consistent findings. After adjustment for covariates, academic stage (pre-clinical vs. clinical) was not significantly associated with empathy.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: ACEs are common among Thai medical students and are independently associated with lower empathy scores. Depressive symptoms were also linked to reduced empathy, whereas current life stress showed a modest but statistically significant positive association, a finding that warrants further investigation. These findings suggest that empathic development during medical training is influenced not only by curricular experiences but also by students' early life experiences and psychological well-being. Integrating trauma-informed and mental health-responsive approaches into medical education may help support both student well-being and empathic clinical practice.

items.title: Bouldering-Psychotherapy for treating depression in adolescents (BooSt): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
items.authors: Luttenberger K, Donath C, Eversmann L, Göttlicher KL, Scheuermann JS, Brokmeier LL, Radegast A, Scheufele P, Lewczuk P, Kiesel V, Kuntscher R, Meyer S, Hulm M, Schwarzkopf L, Eichler A, Kratz O.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Currently, there are hardly any validated group therapy programs for depressed adolescents in Germany. A recent meta-analysis confirmed a moderate antidepressant effect of exercise in adolescents with depressive symptoms. In addition, four recent systematic reviews reported positive effects of exercise interventions on psychological well-being, mood, and quality of life in adolescents with depression or depressive symptoms. We developed a manualized behavioral-therapy-based group program involving Bouldering-Psychotherapy (BPT) for adolescents (BPT-J) based on the adult version of BPT, which has already demonstrated its efficacy. The aim of the study is to evaluate the efficacy of BPT-J.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The study is designed as a randomized, controlled, prospective, longitudinal, single-blind trial with two arms (BPT-J intervention group [IG], waitlist-control group [CG]). The primary aim is to investigate the efficacy of the BPT-J group therapy for adolescents for treating depressiveness. Eligible participants are adolescents with subclinical and clinical depressive symptoms between 13 and 18 years of age. The adolescents in the CG are offered participation in an identical intervention after t1. The 10-week intervention is accompanied by four data collection points for all participants: participants and their legal guardians fill out online questionnaires at the start of therapy (t0), immediately after IG therapy (t1), after CG therapy (t2), and 12 months after finalizing the intervention (follow-up, t3). In addition, structured video interviews are conducted at t0 and t1.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: BooSt trial addresses the limited availability of evidence-based group interventions for adolescents with depressive symptoms in routine care. If efficacy is confirmed, BPT-J may represent a scalable, manualized, and potentially well-accepted treatment approach that could complement existing psychotherapeutic services for adolescents. Given the increasing demand and limited access to psychotherapy, the intervention may contribute to improving accessibility of mental health care. The group-based format may additionally support cost-effective implementation, reduce waiting times, facilitate peer support, and help reduce stigmatization associated with mental health treatment. Findings from the BooSt trial may further inform dissemination and implementation strategies in child and adolescent mental health care.

items.title: Architectures and strategies for the differential diagnosis of adolescent depression and anxiety: bridging tabular deep learning, interpretability, and scale streamlining.
items.authors: Sun R, Wu Y, Luo Z, Zheng Q, Bai Y, Pan X, Ding X, Liu L, Dong G, Guan X.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Escalating societal and occupational pressures have exacerbated the global mental health crisis. The symptomatic overlap between depression and anxiety presents a formidable diagnostic hurdle for differential diagnosis in mental health. developing AI-driven diagnostic models to differentiate these states and streamlining complex clinical instruments is of substantial clinical and scientific value.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Utilizing clinical questionnaires and physician-confirmed diagnoses, distinct datasets were established. This study evaluates four dimensions: model architecture, data strategy optimization, interpretability, and clinical instrument streamlining. Four resampling strategies and tabular generative models were integrated to address data imbalance. Through stratified cross-validation, 29 models-spanning traditional Machine Learning (ML), sequential Deep Learning (DL), and advanced tabular DL-were compared. Optimization strategies focusing on input representation and generalization were also evaluated.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Data strategies significantly enhanced standard deep learning architectures. Specifically, Mambular-TTT combined with Borderline-SMOTE and TVAE achieved a 7.3% relative AUC improvement over the best-performing traditional machine learning baseline. Hierarchical SHAP identified childhood trauma and neuroticism as shared correlated predictive features while revealing subtype-specific feature association patterns. Stepwise reduction revealed that a 7-instrument subset optimally balances diagnostic performance and clinical efficiency; the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) for the streamlined Dataset 2 improved to 0.70, outperforming the full-scale model.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This study demonstrates that reliable AI-assisted diagnosis requires the integrated optimization of model architecture and data strategy. This approach, combined with an interpretability-based scale streamlining strategy, provides a practical and evidence-based implementation path for transforming machine learning models into efficient, deployable clinical diagnostic tools.

This approach, combined with an interpretability-based scale streamlining strategy, provides a practical and evidence-based implementation path for transforming machine learning models into efficient, deployable clinical diagnostic tools.

items.title: Body image, associated stigma as a determinant of depression, anxiety, and stress among adolescents in Salem, Tamil Nadu: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: P S, Krishnamoorthy P, Balasundaram S, Sambasivam I.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Body image shaming is a growing public health concern affecting adolescent mental health. Adolescents face increasing pressure from peers, families, and the media regarding their appearance. Negative comments about appearance have been associated with depression, anxiety, and stress during this critical developmental stage.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: To explore the association between body image shaming and depression, anxiety, and stress among adolescents in Salem, Tamil Nadu.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 310 adolescents aged 10-19 years, selected through multistage random sampling in Salem. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire including socio-demographics, the Body Image Shaming Scale (BISS-20), and the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale (DASS-21). Inferential statistics included chi-square tests to examine associations between categorical variables and binary logistic regression analyses adjusted for gender, BMI category, residence, and education level to assess the independent association between body image shaming and depression, anxiety, and stress.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: High levels of body image shaming were reported by 46.8% of the participants. Mild depression (19.7%), extremely severe anxiety (22.6%), and moderate stress (19.7%) were observed. There was a significant association between body image shaming and depression (χ²=13.5; p = 0.009), anxiety (χ²=41.2; p < 0.001), and stress (χ²=36.78; p < 0.001). BMI was significantly associated with stress (p < 0.02).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Body image shaming is prevalent among adolescents and is strongly associated with adverse mental health outcomes. Awareness campaigns should target both adolescents who experience shaming and those who engage in it, promoting empathy, body positivity, and supportive peer interactions. Targeted interventions, such as awareness campaigns, peer support groups, counselling services, and school-based programs, are essential to address this issue and promote adolescent well-being.

items.title: Multidimensional dietary patterns and cardiometabolic comorbidity in adults with anxiety disorders: evidence from NHANES and linked dietary databases using interpretable machine learning.
items.authors: Yang Q, Lin Q, He Y, Wang Y, Nie X.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Anxiety disorders frequently co-occur with cardiometabolic conditions, yet little is known about how everyday dietary exposures shape cardiovascular vulnerability within this population. Existing studies typically focus on isolated nutrients or single dietary indices, overlooking the broader food environment in which dietary choices are made. This study examined how multiple dimensions of diet including micronutrient intake, dietary patterns and specific food items relate to hypertension-coronary heart disease (CHD) comorbidity among adults with anxiety disorders.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We analyzed data from seven NHANES cycles (2005-2018) to identify adults with anxiety disorders and assess the presence of hypertension-CHD comorbidity. Dietary exposures were evaluated using 24-hour recalls and aggregated across three complementary domains linked to NHANES: core micronutrients, MyPyramid Equivalents for food groups, and WWEIA for individual foods. Multicollinearity was assessed through correlation analysis, followed by feature selection using the Boruta algorithm. Class imbalance was addressed with the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). Six machine learning models were developed and compared. Feature-level associations between dietary micronutrients, daily dietary intake, and food consumption and the risk of hypertension-CHD comorbidity were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME). Model stability was further evaluated through time-series analyses.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Across analytic approaches, several consistent dietary signatures emerged. Higher intakes of vitamin E, polyunsaturated fatty acids, folate, calcium, protein, and total energy were associated with lower odds of comorbidity, whereas zinc and iron intake showed positive associations. Dietary patterns rich in protein foods, poultry, seafood, and vegetables were inversely related to comorbidity, while starchy vegetables and cured meats were associated with increased risk. At the food level, bananas, coffee, cream substitutes, and tomato-based products were linked to lower risk, whereas yeast breads, margarine, cakes, and pies were linked to higher risk. Machine-learning models reinforced these findings and highlighted the cumulative influence of food choices rather than single nutrients.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: In adults with anxiety disorders, we identified clear and consistent dietary patterns associated with the coexistence of hypertension and coronary heart disease. By combining micronutrient intake, dietary patterns, and food-level data with interpretable machine-learning approaches, this study demonstrates that diet may contribute to cardiometabolic vulnerability in this understudied population. These findings highlight diet as a modifiable factor that could be incorporated into broader prevention efforts and support the value of routine dietary assessment in both psychiatric and general healthcare settings.

items.title: Time-Variant Patterns of Comorbid Depression and Anxiety Across Early to Late Adolescence: The Sex-Specific Role of Emotion Regulation.
items.authors: Liu D, Wei X, Jia L, Zhang B.

sections.heading: Aims
sections.text: Depression-anxiety comorbidity is common in adolescence, yet prevention efforts often overlook the nonlinear course of psychosocial development. This study mapped the dynamic risk of depression-anxiety comorbidity across adolescence and examined whether emotion regulation moderated these associations by grade and sex.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We utilised time-varying effect modelling (TVEM) on data of youth from all primary and secondary schools in Chenzhou, China ( n  = 58,622; grades 4-12), to map the dynamic change of comorbid risk and potential moderating role of emotion regulation, with consideration of sex difference. Participants reported depressive and anxiety symptoms through the patient health questionnaire and generalised anxiety disorder questionnaire, respectively. The emotion regulation questionnaire (ERQ) measured two dimensions of emotion regulation, cognitive reappraisal and expression suppression.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Overall comorbid risk increased throughout adolescence. Anxiety (OR = 1.67, 95% CI [1.61, 1.74]) and depressive (OR = 1.68, 95% CI [1.50, 1.89]) symptoms had similar overall comorbid risk, while depression-related risk became stronger than anxiety-related risk in late adolescence. Sex-specific patterns revealed higher comorbid risks in females. A gradual risk progression across grades emerged in males, whereas females showed a steeper increase in depression-associated comorbidity and an anxiety-associated peak around grade 8 (OR = 1.74, 95% CI [1.69, 1.80]). The role of emotion regulation is more pronounced in females than males. Cognitive reappraisal had a protective role against anxiety-related comorbid risk (OR = 0.99, 95% CI [0.99, 0.99]) and a maladaptive role for depression-related comorbid risk (OR = 1.01, 95% CI [1.01, 1.01]). The maladaptive role of expressive suppression for anxiety-associated comorbidity peaked during middle school for females and only emerged during early adolescence for males.

sections.heading: Interpretation
sections.text: Depression-anxiety comorbidity showed distinct grade- and sex-specific risk patterns across adolescence. These findings advocate for precise interventions prioritising anxiety management during primary-to-middle school transition and depression prevention during late adolescence. Emotion regulation interventions should be tailored by sex, adolescence stage and existing symptoms.

items.title: Age-related differences in the mental health burden among Ukrainians during war and forced migration.
items.authors: Larysa S.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Our study focuses on the effects of the stressors of modern conditions of martial law and forced displacement on the state and mental health of Ukrainians adult. The aim of our study is to analyze the state of mental health and wellbeing of Ukrainians during war and forced migration compared, namely to determine the level of the most common mental health problems - depression, anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), as well as resources for overcoming the consequences of stressful influences.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: We developed a conceptual model of the components of mental health and wellbeing, which became the basis for the development of an online questionnaire on the LimeSurvey platform, with using the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5), the Life Events Checklist for DSM-5 (LEC-5), the Refugee Post-Migration Stress Scale (RPMS), the Brief Symptom Inventory Derogatis (BSI-18), block of open-ended socio-demographic issues, and SPSS Statistics 21.0.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The sample comprised 306 Ukrainian participants. Participants were grouped by age: under 26 years and 26 years or older; and place of residence: 1) "lives in another country;" 2) "lives in Ukraine, moved;" 3) "lives in Ukraine, did not move." Differences in symptom scores were observed between subgroups, with the smallest subgroup interpreted cautiously. Among Ukrainian people affected by armed conflicts and migrants, the most common mental disorders (CMDs), such as depression, anxiety disorders and post-traumatic stress disorder, constitute a significant proportion of serious illnesses worldwide. The results obtained in our study confirm this trend also among Ukrainians, who are currently experiencing all the difficulties of wartime.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: The findings provide a descriptive comparison of psychological symptoms and perceived coping resources across different age and residential groups of Ukrainians adult in the condition of war. Resource-oriented to mental health assessment and intervention for war-affected populations is important, contributing to understanding adaptive functioning in the context of protracted armed conflict and may nevertheless inform future research and support planning for war-affected populations.

items.title: The Mediating Role of Sleep Quality in Associations of Smartphone Addiction and Time-Specific Use With Prenatal Depression and Anxiety: Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
items.authors: Zhang X, Ouyang M, Wu X, Yang X, Wang X, Cao Y, Xu M, Shu Y, Wu M.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Prenatal depression and anxiety have emerged as pressing global public health challenges. In the digital era, excessive smartphone use may exert complex effects on maternal mental health. Prior research has predominantly focused on adolescents, whereas evidence among pregnant women, particularly regarding total weekly use and use during critical circadian windows, such as after waking and before bedtime, remains limited. Furthermore, the mediating role of sleep quality in these associations has yet to be systematically examined.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to investigate the associations of smartphone addiction and time-specific smartphone use with prenatal depression and anxiety, and to assess the mediating role of sleep quality in these associations.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional observational study enrolled 537 pregnant women. Smartphone use characteristics, sleep quality, and prenatal depression and anxiety were assessed using the Smartphone Addiction Scale-Short Version (SAS-SV), objective total weekly smartphone use recorded by the device, and self-reported duration of smartphone use after waking and duration of bedtime smartphone use; the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), respectively. Binary logistic regression was used to estimate associations, restricted cubic spline (RCS) models were used to explore nonlinear patterns, and exploratory mediation analyses were used to examine whether sleep quality statistically accounted for part of the observed associations.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The prevalence of moderate-to-severe prenatal depression and anxiety was 8.8% (47/537) and 5.8% (31/537), respectively. After adjusting for covariates, smartphone addiction was associated with higher odds of depression (odds ratio [OR] 3.461, 95% CI 1.771-7.100) and anxiety (OR 7.738, 95% CI 3.064-23.172). Duration of smartphone use after waking ≥61 minutes and duration of bedtime smartphone use ≥91 minutes were also associated with higher odds of affective disorders. RCS analyses further revealed distinct nonlinear patterns across different exposure dimensions: duration of smartphone use after waking displayed U-shaped and J-shaped associations with depression and anxiety, respectively, while total weekly use displayed a U-shaped association with anxiety. Exploratory mediation analyses showed that the indirect pathways through sleep quality were statistically significant for the associations of bedtime smartphone use, weekly smartphone use, and smartphone addiction with prenatal depression, with mediation proportions of 44.89% (0.0065/0.0145), 31.30% (0.0056/0.0183), and 31.48% (0.0415/0.1315), respectively. The corresponding proportions in the anxiety models were 35.83% (0.0044/0.0123), 27.05% (0.0039/0.0144), and 22.73% (0.0271/0.1187).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Smartphone addiction and excessive smartphone use after waking and before bedtime were associated with higher odds of prenatal depression and anxiety. Sleep quality may statistically account for part of these associations, but longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporal ordering and causal pathways.

items.title: Social Media Use Motives and Mental Health Among Adolescents: Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Lian J, Künzi M, Andrews JL, Gallacher J, Bauermeister S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Social media use is ubiquitous among young people, yet its relationship with mental health may depend on why it is used. Understanding the motives underlying social media engagement may provide greater insights into its potential risks and benefits than considering overall use alone.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to identify latent dimensions of motives for social media use and examine their associations with anxiety, depression, well-being, and resilience in a sample of older adolescents.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Cross-sectional data were drawn from the BrainWaves study (N=6820; mean age 16.72, SD 0.74 years). Social media use motives were assessed using 10 items and exploratory factor analysis identified 2 latent dimensions: avoidant-escapist use (boredom, addiction, distraction, and procrastination) and social-recreational use (socializing, communication, entertainment, and observation). Confirmatory factor analysis was used to estimate factor scores, which were examined using linear regression. Structural equation modeling estimated associations with anxiety, depression, well-being, and resilience, with secondary analyses accounting for gender and deprivation.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Linear regression analyses showed that avoidant-escapist motives were associated with higher anxiety and depressive symptoms, whereas social-recreational motives were associated with lower symptoms. No interactions with gender or deprivation were observed. The structural equation model showed acceptable model fit (comparative fit index=0.945; root mean squared error of approximation=0.057; standardized root mean squared residual=0.054). Avoidant-escapist motives were associated with higher anxiety (β=0.543) and depressive symptoms (β=0.629) and lower well-being (β=-0.610) and resilience (β=-0.469). Conversely, social-recreational motives were associated with lower anxiety (β=-0.228) and depressive symptoms (β=-0.342) and higher well-being (β=0.362) and resilience (β=0.242; P <.001 in all cases). These patterns remained consistent after accounting for gender and deprivation.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Social media use shows different associations with older adolescent mental health depending on underlying motives. Focusing on why young people engage with social media rather than on overall use alone may provide a more informative framework for understanding potential risks and benefits. Given the cross-sectional design, causal inferences cannot be made.

items.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Treatment Pattern and Its Associated Outcomes Among Children Referred to Psychiatry and Mental Health Services in Malaysia: Protocol for a Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.authors: Muhamad NA, Ling LS, Maamor NH, Hussin S, Tengku Baharudin Shah TPN, Jamalluddin NH, Leman FN, Musa NSE, Yahya F, Chemi N, Abdullah N, Abdul Jabbar N, Ibrahim N.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder associated with significant impairments in academic, social, and daily functioning. Despite the availability of clinical practice guidelines in Malaysia, evidence on real-world treatment patterns and outcomes remains limited. The lack of multicenter data on treatment use and clinical outcomes hinders the evaluation of current ADHD care and opportunities for service improvement.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: The primary objective of this study is to observe treatment patterns among children with ADHD referred to psychiatry and mental health services in Malaysia after receiving treatment for 18 months. This study will also compare treatment outcomes between children with ADHD who do receive treatment and those who do not receive any ADHD treatment.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This multicenter retrospective cohort study will use secondary data from clinical records of children aged 4 to 16 years with a confirmed diagnosis of ADHD. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, clinical features, ADHD subtype and comorbidities, treatment modalities, health care use, treatment trajectories, and clinical outcomes will be extracted using a standardized case report form and will be anonymized prior to analysis. Data collection will be undertaken by trained site investigators and medical officers across participating centers. Statistical analyses will be conducted using R software (R Foundation for Statistical Computing). Descriptive statistics will be used to summarize characteristics, treatment patterns, health care use, and clinical outcomes of children with ADHD. Treatment patterns will be characterized according to pharmacological and nonpharmacological interventions, treatment modifications, and service use. Comparative analyses will be performed to examine associations between treatment patterns and clinical outcomes across children with ADHD and clinical subgroups.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: This study will be funded through a Ministry of Health Research Grant obtained in August 2026. It will commence in August 2026 and end in December 2028. Based on the sample size calculation, a minimum of 2771 eligible children with ADHD records will be included in the study. items.title: Smoking cessation experiences during alcohol and cannabis treatment in substance use programmes in Catalonia: A qualitative study.
items.authors: Rosa N, Enríquez M, Saura J, Feliu A, Roca X, Andreu M, Raich A, Fernández E, Martínez C.
items.journal: Substance abuse treatment, prevention, and policy

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Tobacco use remains disproportionately high among people receiving treatment for alcohol or cannabis use, yet it is rarely addressed in substance use services. This study explored the lived experiences of people who smoke while undergoing treatment for alcohol and/or cannabis use, aiming to identify barriers and facilitators to integrating tobacco cessation into public substance use services.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This phenomenological study formed part of the qualitative phase of an observational follow-up investigation conducted in Catalonia (Spain) with people receiving treatment for alcohol and/or cannabis use. In-depth, semi-structured video interviews were conducted with nine adults (seven men, two women; aged 22-67 years) attending Centres for the Care and Follow-up of Substance Use Disorders. Data were collected between May and October 2024 and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Five interconnected themes captured participants' experiences: (1) Tobacco use dynamics-smoking was perceived as an emotional regulator, ingrained habit, and possible substitute during abstinence from other substances; (2) Processes of reflection and change- participants favoured gradual, sequential approaches to cessation and reported heightened health awareness when reducing tobacco use; (3) Support networks and interpersonal relationships-family support and strong clinical alliances facilitated motivation, whereas inconsistent professional follow-up undermined it; (4) Stigma and social perceptions-internalised and external stigma about smoking and substance use shaped participants' attitudes toward quitting; and (5) Sustainability and relapse prevention strategies-continued professional support, access to affordable pharmacotherapy, and smoke-free environments were viewed as essential, yet often unavailable.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Participants endorsed addressing tobacco cessation in alcohol and cannabis treatment but reported multiple structural, financial, and attitudinal barriers within public substance use services. Systematically integrating tobacco assessment, personalised counselling, and subsidised pharmacological support into these programmes could enhance cessation outcomes and potentially improve recovery outcomes for co-occurring substance use disorders. Findings support policy initiatives aimed at embedding comprehensive tobacco cessation pathways in Spanish addiction services.

items.title: Eating disorder-related attitudes as predictors of pre-frailty/frailty in older adults: a cross-sectional clinical study.
items.authors: Çıtar Dazıroğlu ME, Akpınar Şentüre Ş, Çataltepe E, Çeker E, Fadıloğlu A, Varan HD, Acar Tek N.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Frailty is a prevalent geriatric syndrome influenced by nutritional status, body composition, and functional capacity. Nevertheless, the role of eating disorder-related attitudes and behaviors in older adults is not definitively known. Therefore, this study was conducted to investigate the association between frailty and eating disorder-related attitudes and behaviors in older adults.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study included 79 older adults (73.2 ± 6.14 years) attending a geriatric outpatient clinic. Frailty was assessed using the Frailty score, and participants were classified as non-frail or pre-frail/frail. Eating disorder-related attitudes were evaluated using the Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire (EDE-Q). Anthropometric measurements, body composition assessed by bioelectrical impedance analysis, and handgrip strength were obtained. Spearman correlation and logistic regression analyses were performed.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Pre-frail/frail individuals had significantly higher scores for thoughts about body shape and weight compared with non-frail participants (p = 0.029). Disordered eating behaviors showed positive correlations with visceral fat and body mass index (BMI), while body fat percentage was positively correlated with the frailty score (p < 0.05). Furthermore, logistic regression analysis showed that higher total EDE-Q scores were associated with higher odds of frailty risk (p = 0.036).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Eating disorder-related attitudes may be associated with increased frailty risk in older adults, highlighting the potential importance of integrating disordered eating assessments into geriatric evaluation.

items.title: Associations among caregiving burden, social support, hope, mastery, and depressive symptoms in family caregivers of children and young people with mental illness: a chain mediation analysis.
items.authors: Guan Z, Yao H, Li K, Sun W, Peng Y, Chen JYC, Cong E, Cheng W, Chen J, Xu Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Caregiving burden and depressive symptoms are common among family caregivers of children and young people (CYP) with mental illness, but the interplay among psychosocial and coping resources are not well understood. This cross-sectional study aimed to assess the relationship between caregiving burden and depressive symptoms and the roles of social support, hope, and mastery in this relationship among Chinese family caregivers of CYP with mental illness.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Totally 333 Chinese family caregivers of CYP with mental illness were recruited, who completed the 12-item Zarit Burden Interview, the 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire, Oslo 3-item Social Support Scale, the Herth Hope Index, and the Pearlin Mastery Scale between September 2024 and February 2025. Descriptive analysis, correlation analysis, and the PROCESS Macro model 6 in regression analysis were applied.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Results showed that 63.7% of participants reported caregiving burden and 48.0% reported moderate to severe depressive symptoms. Moreover, caregiving burden (r = 0.652, p < 0.001), social support (r = -0.392, p < 0.001), mastery (r = -0.500, p < 0.001), and hope (r = -0.507, p < 0.001) were related to depressive symptoms. Importantly, social support, hope, and mastery formed multiple indirect pathways between caregiving burden and depressive symptoms.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Mental healthcare workers should be aware that majority of family caregivers experience caregiving burden and depressive symptoms, and that programs enhancing family caregivers' social support, hope, and mastery should be considered to support these family caregivers.

items.title: Pathways to medication adherence: a configurational analysis of psychiatric symptoms and medication attitude in patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorder receiving long-acting injectable antipsychotics.
items.authors: Zhang L, Chen Y, Yu H, Sun Y, Li Q, Zhang S, Jiang W, Luo F, Zhou Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Medication non-adherence affects nearly half of patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorder and is associated with relapse and hospitalization. Long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics may improve adherence, but their effectiveness likely depends on interactions between specific psychiatric symptom patterns and medication attitudes. This study, a secondary analysis of published data from the Dryad repository, examined how configurations of psychiatric symptoms factors influence adherence via medication attitude among patients receiving LAI.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This secondary analysis included 304 patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorder (mean age 45.64 years; 63.16% male) receiving LAI from Italy. We employed complex mediation qualitative comparative analysis (cmQCA) to examine symptom-adherence pathways. Psychiatric symptoms were assessed using the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale-18 items (BPRS-18) across five dimensions: affect, positive symptoms, negative symptoms, resistance, and activation. Medication attitudes were evaluated with the Drug Attitude Inventory (DAI-10), and adherence was measured using Kemp's 7-point scale. Regression models examined direct and mediated relationships, controlling for demographic variables, substance abuse history, LAI generation, and injection interval.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) identified six configurations: three promoting positive medication attitudes (46% solution coverage, 82% consistency) and three leading to poor medication attitudes (39.5% coverage, 79.4% consistency) characterized by high Resistance. The absence of Positive Symptoms and Resistance emerged as core conditions for positive medication attitudes. Regression analyses confirmed partial mediation through medication attitudes.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Multiple pathways link psychiatric symptom configurations to medication adherence through medication attitude in patients receiving LAI treatment. Clinicians should consider specific symptom patterns for adherence interventions. Targeted approaches addressing both symptom configurations and medication attitudes may optimize outcomes for schizophrenia spectrum disorder.

items.title: Network analysis of mental health literacy among adolescents and comparison of gender differences.
items.authors: Jiang Z, Li Y, Wei W, Zhu J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Mental health literacy serves as a crucial protective factor for adolescents when coping with psychological distress. To deeply investigate the structural characteristics of adolescents' mental health literacy, this study employed network analysis to construct the network structure of adolescents' mental health literacy, identify core nodes, and compare gender differences.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A stratified random sampling method with grade as the classification variable was adopted to select 1,977 adolescents from grades 4 to 9 in Guangdong, China, to conduct the Adolescent Mental Health Literacy Scale survey.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: (1) The results of overall network estimation and inference showed that HS5 ("Talking improves mental health") in the help-seeking dimension had the highest expected influence index, followed by KMH1 ("Thoughts affect feelings") and KMI2 ("Mental disorders affect emotions"), indicating that these three nodes exerted the greatest influence on the item network. (2) The network comparison results demonstrated a significant difference between males and females in the invariance test of global strength (Male = 6.98, Female = 6.42; global strength difference = 0.56, p = 0.04). In the male network, the top three nodes in terms of expected influence index from high to low were HS3 ("Would disclose mental disorder"), HS1 ("Seek help if problems"), and HS4 ("Comfortable sharing with peers"). In the female network, the top three nodes in terms of expected influence index from high to low were HS5 ("Talking improves mental health"), KMI2 ("Mental disorders affect emotions"), and KMH1 ("Thoughts affect feelings").

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The core node of adolescents' mental health literacy is HS5 ("Talking about my feelings with others helps promote mental health"). Further gender-specific analysis revealed that the core node of mental health literacy for male adolescents was HS3 ("I would actively seek help if I have psychological problems") in the help-seeking dimension, while for female adolescents, it was HS5 ("Talking about my feelings with others helps promote mental health") in the help-seeking dimension. Focusing on the help-seeking factor may be a significant intervention direction for enhancing adolescents' mental health literacy.

items.title: "One counselling strategy does not fit all": Midwives' experiences of providing contraceptive counselling to girls and young women with ADHD - a Swedish qualitative interview study.
items.authors: Johansson M, Haglund A, Asplin N.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Despite accessible services, unmet contraceptive needs persist among young women in Sweden. Young women with ADHD may have diverse sexual and reproductive health needs, and previous research has identified challenges related to healthcare access, communication, and contraceptive use. However, less is known about how midwives experience providing contraceptive counselling to girls and young women with ADHD. This study aimed to describe midwives' experiences of providing contraceptive counselling to girls and young women with ADHD in Swedish youth clinics.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A qualitative exploratory study design using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis of interviews, including ten midwives providing contraceptive counselling to young women with ADHD. The average interview time was 34 min.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The participating midwives were aged 31 to 62 years and had between six months and 24 years of experience working in youth clinics across four of Sweden's six healthcare regions. Their experiences were captured by the overarching theme, Adapting contraceptive counselling to individual needs despite limited ADHD-specific support, which encompassed three themes: Striving to provide person-centered counselling, Navigating counselling in response to increased support needs, and Recognizing the importance of ADHD-specific knowledge and resources to support counselling.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Midwives described adapting contraceptive counselling to perceived individual needs through changes in communication, consultation structures, access to care, and interprofessional collaboration. They also described a need for stronger ADHD-specific education and evidence-informed professional guidance. Support for counselling should provide a structured professional foundation while allowing flexibility to respond to individual circumstances and preferences.

items.title: Evaluating the introduction module of Mentalization-Based Treatment: a naturalistic pre-post clinical cohort study.
items.authors: Bachrach N, Brugman S, Berkers R, van der Linde R.
items.journal: Borderline personality disorder and emotion dysregulation

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Mentalization-Based Treatment Introduction (MBT-I) is a psychoeducational group module preceding long-term Mentalization-Based Treatment (MBT) for patients with borderline personality disorder (BPD). MBT-I aims to increase knowledge of mentalizing and BPD, prepare patients for treatment, clarify diagnosis, and assess mentalizing capacities. However, empirical evidence remains limited. This study examined whether MBT-I was associated with improved mentalizing capacity and attainment of its clinical goals.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A naturalistic, non-randomized one-group pre-post study was conducted in a Dutch mental health care institute. Patients attended ten weekly MBT-I group sessions. Of 60 patients included, 51 were analyzed. Most had a primary BPD diagnosis; others had personality disorders with comparable difficulties in relational functioning, self-image, and mentalizing. Mentalizing capacity was assessed using the Reflective Functioning Questionnaire, Interpersonal Reactivity Index, and Toronto Alexithymia Scale. MBT-I goals were measured using visual analogue scales.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A trend was found for the TAS-20 subscale 'Difficulty Identifying Feelings'. No significant differences were found between pre- and posttest on the RFQ, IRI, and the remaining subscales of the TAS-20. Significant differences were found comparing pre- and post-VAS scores with regard to the goals of MBT-I.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: MBT-I was not associated with statistically significant improvements across the outcome scales on mentalizing, but a promising trend emerged toward improved emotional awareness. The brief module appears to strengthen early prerequisites for mentalizing and offers clear psychoeducational value by increasing patient knowledge, rather than inducing changes in mentalizing. Future controlled studies are needed to clarify its incremental clinical benefit.

items.title: Training and Experiential Factors Associated With Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Referral Readiness Among Psychiatric Providers.
items.authors: Rahangdale A, Ferraro L, Wood G, Wadsworth C, Venable E.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is an established treatment for patients with treatment-resistant depression (TRD); however, barriers remain in clinical practice. This study examined how psychiatric clinicians view TMS and evaluated whether training exposure and prior experience were associated with their readiness to refer patients for treatment.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of psychiatric providers in Florida, including attending psychiatrists, psychiatry residents, and psychiatric nurse practitioners. The survey assessed beliefs about TMS effectiveness, comfort discussing and referring the treatment, familiarity with referral processes, and perceived barriers. Responses were dichotomized to reflect endorsement, and group differences were analyzed using chi-square or Fisher exact tests.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Ninety-four clinicians completed the survey. Conceptual endorsement of TMS was high, with more than 90% agreeing that it is an effective treatment for depression. Operational readiness was more variable, particularly for referral comfort, counseling confidence, and knowledge of referral pathways. Prior TMS training and prior TMS recommendation experience were associated with greater comfort referring patients, greater confidence counseling patients, and higher awareness of referral steps. Psychiatry residents reported lower referral-pathway awareness than attending psychiatrists. Insurance coverage and treatment costs were frequently reported barriers, and lack of training was a commonly endorsed modifiable barrier.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: While psychiatric providers widely accepted TMS conceptually, operational readiness to counsel and refer was more variable. Training exposure and prior TMS recommendation experience were associated with greater confidence, comfort, and familiarity with referral pathways, although causality cannot be inferred from this cross-sectional design. These findings suggest that efforts to improve utilization should emphasize building operational competence and confidence, along with clearer referral workflows and accessible system-level processes.

We conducted a cross-sectional survey of psychiatric providers in Florida, including attending psychiatrists, psychiatry residents, and psychiatric nurse practitioners. The survey assessed beliefs about TMS effectiveness, comfort discussing and referring the treatment, familiarity with referral processes, and perceived barriers. Responses were dichotomized to reflect endorsement, and group differences were analyzed using chi-square or Fisher exact tests.

Ninety-four clinicians completed the survey. Conceptual endorsement of TMS was high, with more than 90% agreeing that it is an effective treatment for depression. Operational readiness was more variable, particularly for referral comfort, counseling confidence, and knowledge of referral pathways. Prior TMS training and prior TMS recommendation experience were associated with greater comfort referring patients, greater confidence counseling patients, and higher awareness of referral steps. Psychiatry residents reported lower referral-pathway awareness than attending psychiatrists. Insurance coverage and treatment costs were frequently reported barriers, and lack of training was a commonly endorsed modifiable barrier.

While psychiatric providers widely accepted TMS conceptually, operational readiness to counsel and refer was more variable. Training exposure and prior TMS recommendation experience were associated with greater confidence, comfort, and familiarity with referral pathways, although causality cannot be inferred from this cross-sectional design. These findings suggest that efforts to improve utilization should emphasize building operational competence and confidence, along with clearer referral workflows and accessible system-level processes.

items.title: Risk prediction models for non-suicidal self-injury in adolescents with depression: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Xie X, Li Y, Li H, Gan T, Huang L, Cheng J.
items.journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is prevalent among adolescents with depression and is a significant predictor of suicidal behavior. Although several risk prediction models for NSSI have been developed, their overall performance, methodological quality, and feasibility for clinical translation remain unclear.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the performance of NSSI risk prediction models for adolescents with depression through a systematic review and meta-analysis, summarize their area under the curve (AUC) values, and determine the incidence of NSSI and associated predictors in this population.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: PubMed, Web of Science, The Cochrane Library, CINAHL, Embase, Scopus, PsycINFO, CNKI, and Wanfang Database were searched from inception to September 20, 2025. The GRADE approach, PROBAST, and TRIPOD tools were used to assess the overall certainty of evidence, risk of bias, and reporting quality, respectively. Data were extracted using the CHARMS checklist. The PROBAST and TRIPOD tools were used to assess the risk of bias and reporting quality, respectively. Meta-analyses of model AUC values and NSSI incidence were performed using Stata 17.0.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Eighteen studies (comprising 40 models) were included. The meta-analysis revealed a pooled NSSI incidence of 50% (95% CI = 0.29-0.71) among adolescents with depression. The models demonstrated promising discriminative ability: the pooled AUC was 0.82 (95% CI = 0.79-0.86) for development cohorts, 0.90 (95% CI = 0.87-0.93) for internal validation cohorts, and 0.82 (95% CI = 0.77-0.86) for external validation cohorts. The most frequently identified predictors included depression severity, childhood trauma, sex, emotional abuse, and emotional neglect. However, the PROBAST assessment revealed a high risk of bias in most studies, particularly in the domains of participant selection and statistical analysis. The TRIPOD assessment indicated insufficient reporting of key methodological details such as sample size justification and handling of missing data. Only five studies conducted external validation. The certainty of evidence assessed by GRADE was low to very low for the main outcomes, mainly because of high risk of bias, substantial heterogeneity, indirectness, and limited validation evidence.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Existing prediction models show promising discriminative potential for identifying NSSI risk in adolescents with depression. However, high AUC values should be interpreted cautiously because methodological bias, substantial heterogeneity, limited external validation, incomplete reporting, and population differences may have led to overly optimistic performance estimates. Future research should focus on building more robust, trustworthy, and clinically translatable tools through prospective designs, adequate sample sizes, standardized analytical methods, extensive external validation, and complete reporting adhering to the TRIPOD guidelines.
