items.title: When the clinician becomes the manager: safety planning as intrapsychic enactment and a testable Internal Family Systems reframing of suicide-specific care.
items.authors: Strobel J.

sections.text: Safety planning depends on disclosure. Yet many suicidal patients conceal their suicidal intent from clinicians, often fearing the consequences of disclosure. Critics of contemporary suicide-prevention frameworks increasingly warn that a detection-and-containment approach may foster a defensive, algorithmic practice, but an encounter-level account of how such an approach may become counter-therapeutic has remained underdeveloped. Drawing on Internal Family Systems (IFS) theory, we propose one such account. We argue that suicidality is often best understood as a protective response to unbearable distress, conceptualized within IFS as a "firefighter" stance: a protective action whose catastrophic outcome nonetheless serves a function. More novelly, we suggest that containment-oriented safety planning can recruit the clinician into the `manager' role within the patient's internal system, recreating within the therapeutic dyad the very manager-firefighter polarity that may contribute to the crisis. From this follows a specific paradox: a system that depends on disclosure may, under certain conditions, suppress the very disclosure on which it relies. The contribution of this paper is neither the functional interpretation of suicidality nor the critique of containment-oriented care, both of which are well established in the literature. Rather, it is the proposal that the clinical encounter itself may operate as an enactment of the patient's own manager-firefighter polarity, and that it may create a concealment mechanism through which suppression-oriented care may undermine its own aims. From this account, we derive a falsifiable prediction that distinguishes it from alliance- and autonomy-based explanations: a containment-oriented approach should produce selective concealment of suicidal intent despite preserved engagement-a dissociation between sustained alliance and concealed suicidal intent that those explanations do not predict. Conditions for disconfirmation are specified.

items.title: Cross-sectional assessment of anxiety and insomnia of Spanish veterinarians following African swine fever wild boar detection in Spain.
items.authors: Schambow RA, Guerra P, Aviles MM, Iglesias I, Yagüe AP, Higuera MA, Perez AD, Perez AM.

sections.text: In November 2025, African swine fever (ASF) was detected in wild boar in the Catalonia region of Spain. The primary objective of this cross-sectional survey study was to descriptively explore the mental health impacts of the emergence of ASF in Spain on Spanish practicing veterinarians working with swine and to provide a baseline for future comparison if conditions of the ASF epidemic in Spain significantly change. A questionnaire with the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 and Insomnia Severity Index was distributed via convenience sampling to Spanish pig veterinarians from April to May 2026. Working in an ASF control zone, and working in Catalonia, were primary exposures of interest for anxiety and insomnia score. Data were analyzed using univariate analyses. Fifty-three veterinarians responded to the survey. Median anxiety score was 6.00 (interquartile range [IQR]: 2.00-10.0) and median insomnia score was 8.00 (IQR: 4.00-13.0). Some veterinarians reported new feelings of uneasiness or sadness (54.7%), extreme changes in their feelings of happiness and sadness (41.5%), and less confidence in their abilities or their value (41.5%) since the ASF outbreak. Working in an ASF control zone or working in Catalonia were not significantly associated with insomnia or anxiety score ( p  > 0.05). These findings help to describe the current status of anxiety and insomnia amongst Spanish pig veterinarians following the ASF detection in wild boar, and provide a baseline for future comparisons if the ASF epidemic worsens in the country.

items.title: Financial Functioning Before Mental Health Disclosure to a Retail Bank.
items.authors: Trendl A, Bremner G, Harrison J, Llewellyn DJ, Leake D.

sections.heading: Importance
sections.text: Financial functioning is an important dimension of mental health, affecting independence and overall functioning. However, there is uncertainty about how financial functioning evolves over time and across mental health conditions, with current evidence largely relying on survey or experimental data.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To evaluate whether financial functioning differs in the period preceding mental health disclosure to a bank and whether differences are shared or condition specific.

sections.heading: Design, setting, and participants
sections.text: In this case-control study, deidentified banking records from a major UK bank were used to compare financial indicators between individuals with a bank-disclosed mental health condition between January 2019 and August 2025 and controls, matched 1:3. Analyses were conducted between July 2025 and March 2026.

sections.heading: Exposures
sections.text: Bank-recorded mental health disclosures mapped to diagnostic groupings of mental, behavioral, and neurodevelopmental conditions.

sections.heading: Main outcomes and measures
sections.text: A total of 331 monthly financial indicators were used to capture financial functioning. A 2-stage bayesian hierarchical model examined how variation in case-control differences was distributed across financial indicators, conditions, and their interaction.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The case group comprised 18 428 individuals with mental health disclosures (mean [SD] age, 41.5 [13.9] years; 10 357 women [56%]) and the control group included 64 229 individuals (mean [SD] age, 40.9 [14.5] years; 36 052 women [56%]). Differences in financial functioning were evident up to 36 months before disclosure. Compared with controls, posterior mean estimates for cases showed higher welfare-related income (disability benefits: 0.80; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.78-0.83), greater financial distress (credit scores: -0.52 [95% CrI, -0.55 to -0.49]; overdraft use: 0.49 [95% CrI, 0.47-0.52]), and more frequent bank interaction (eg, telephone banking use: 0.56 [95% CrI, 0.53-0.58]). Additional differences included higher cash use and reduced spending on self-care and recreational activities among cases (standardized differences ≤0.4 SD units). Variance decomposition indicated that most variation was attributable to differences across financial indicators (SD, 0.11; 88% of total variance), with negligible variation explained by condition (SD, 0.01; <1%) and a small contribution from interaction effects (SD, 0.04; 12%), indicating broadly consistent patterns across conditions.

sections.heading: Conclusions and relevance
sections.text: In this case-control study of bank customers, those who disclosed a mental health condition differed from controls across a range of financial indicators preceding the disclosure, with similar patterns across conditions. The findings suggest that banking data may provide objective measures of financial functioning to inform support strategies in banking and clinical contexts.

items.title: Psychometric properties of the Farsi version of the Night Eating Disorder Questionnaire.
items.authors: Khalkhali M, Fatemi S, Yazdanipour M, Khalkhali P.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study assesses the factor structure and psychometric properties of Farsi version of Night Eating Questionnaire.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this cross-sectional study, we randomly selected 155 people referred to Shafa hospital and private psychiatry clinic in Rasht City, Iran. After translation to Farsi and back-translation to English, the face and content validity of NEQ Farsi version were evaluated using the opinions of a panel of experts and calculating the content validity ratio and content validity index. Then, the construct validity was evaluated by Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), the Cronbach α coefficient was used for assessing internal consistency and the Intra class Correlation Coefficient (ICC) was used for assessing test-retest reliability.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The mean age of participants was 41.1 ± 12.9 Years. The CFA results showed that the four-factor model had a good fit. Cronbach's alpha showed an overall coefficient of 0.72. Spearman's correlation coefficient was 0.97 and the intra-class correlation coefficient was 0.99 (95% CI 0.97-0.99), indicating a satisfactory level of test-retest reliability.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The Farsi version of the NEQ has acceptable psychometric properties for the Farsi language and Iranian culture, to be used as a valid and reliable tool in future research, care, and therapeutic activities.

items.title: Differential resting-state functional connectivity of anterior and posterior cerebellar divisions with canonical networks in PTSD.
items.authors: Tunstall L, Steele N, Hussain A, Russell C, Beakas J, Huggins AA, Stevens JS, Ressler K, Jovanovic T, van Rooij SJH, Fani N, Daniels JK, Sierk A, Manthey A, Walter H, Grupe DW, Nitschke JB, Davidson RJ, Baugh LA, Simons RM, Simons JS, Magnotta VA, Fercho KA, Zhu Y, Li G, Wang L, Morey RA, Sun D.
items.journal: Journal of mood and anxiety disorders

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a complex psychiatric condition that may develop following exposure to a singular or series of traumatic events producing disruptions in cognitive and affective processes. Although the cerebellum is traditionally linked to voluntary movement coordination and balance, recent work highlights posterior cerebellar regions are involved in affective and cognitive functions. Our goal was to investigate functional connectivity between the cerebellum and canonical cortical resting-state networks in PTSD, with a particular focus on the posterior cerebellum based on previously reported structural changes associated with PTSD on the posterior cerebellum.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 313 participants ( Mage = 35, 218 females) were comprised of two groups; 119 PTSD patients and 194 healthy controls from eight study sites within the ENIGMA-PTSD working group. The cerebellum was segmented using ACAPULCO into posterior and anterior divisions. Resting-state fMRI preprocessed with HALFpipe was used to assess the functional connectivity of the anterior and posterior divisions of the cerebellum with major canonical cortical networks.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Compared to the non-PTSD control group, the PTSD group had greater connectivity of the posterior cerebellum with somatomotor (t = 4.32, p = 0.040) and default mode (t = 4.41, p = 0.040) networks. Correspondingly, PTSD symptom severity was linked to greater connectivity differentially affecting the posterior relative to the anterior cerebellum with major cortical networks. PTSD symptom severity was positively associated with greater posterior cerebellum connectivity with the default mode (t = 4.32, p_fdr=0.020), somatomotor (t = 3.57, p_fdr=0.040), limbic (t = 3.74, p_fdr=0.036), salience (t = 3.61, p_fdr=0.040) and central executive network (t = 3.59, p_fdr=0.040).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: PTSD symptom severity is associated with altered connectivity of the posterior cerebellum with default mode, salience and central executive networks. Cortical connections with the posterior cerebellum, an important socioemotional hub, are involved in PTSD pathology.

items.title: Sex-Related Differences in Regional Homogeneity and Intolerance of Uncertainty in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: A Resting-State fMRI Study.
items.authors: Wang A, Zhao S, Guo Q, Wu J, Fang W, Zheng S, Zhu C, Zhang X.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) is a cognitive vulnerability associated with symptom severity in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Evidence also suggests that IU and OCD symptom profiles may differ by sex; however, the neural correlates of IU in male and female patients with OCD remain insufficiently characterized.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this cross-sectional observational study, 63 patients with OCD and 40 healthy controls (HCs) underwent resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. Regional homogeneity (ReHo) was used to examine diagnosis- and sex-related differences in intrinsic brain activity. Imaging data were analyzed using a full-factorial model in SPM, with diagnosis and sex as factors and age, years of education, and mean framewise displacement (FD) as covariates. Statistical significance was defined using a voxel-level threshold of p < 0.001 followed by cluster-level family-wise error (FWE) correction at p < 0.05. Significant effects were characterized using post hoc contrasts. Four exploratory partial correlations controlling for age, years of education, and mean FD were examined; their p values were not corrected for multiple comparisons.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The final sample comprised 63 patients with OCD (37 males and 26 females) and 40 HCs (25 males and 15 females). Patients with OCD showed lower ReHo in visual processing regions, including the right calcarine cortex and right middle occipital gyrus, compared with HCs. Across diagnostic groups, the whole-brain factorial analysis revealed a significant main effect of sex, with males showing higher ReHo in visual and sensorimotor regions and females showing higher ReHo in prefrontal regions. No significant diagnosis-by-sex interaction was observed. Exploratory partial correlations showed that higher IU was associated with lower ReHo in the left inferior frontal gyrus in the female OCD, and that lower ReHo in the right middle occipital gyrus was associated with greater obsession severity in the overall OCD sample. These uncorrected associations are preliminary and hypothesis-generating.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings suggest potential sex-related differences in regional neural synchrony in OCD and identify an exploratory association between IU and left inferior frontal gyrus ReHo within the female OCD subgroup. abstract.text:
Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) is a cognitive vulnerability associated with symptom severity in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Evidence also suggests that IU and OCD symptom profiles may differ by sex; however, the neural correlates of IU in male and female patients with OCD remain insufficiently characterized.

In this cross-sectional observational study, 63 patients with OCD and 40 healthy controls (HCs) underwent resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. Imaging data were analyzed using a full-factorial model in SPM, with diagnosis and sex as factors and age, years of education, and mean framewise displacement (FD) as covariates. Statistical significance was defined using a voxel-level threshold of p < 0.001 followed by cluster-level family-wise error (FWE) correction at p < 0.05. Significant effects were characterized using post hoc contrasts. Four exploratory partial correlations controlling for age, years of education, and mean FD were examined; their p values were not corrected for multiple comparisons.

Patients with OCD showed lower ReHo in visual processing regions, including the right calcarine cortex and right middle occipital gyrus, compared with HCs. Across diagnostic groups, the whole-brain factorial analysis revealed a significant main effect of sex, with males showing higher ReHo in visual and sensorimotor regions and females showing higher ReHo in prefrontal regions. No significant diagnosis-by-sex interaction was observed. Exploratory partial correlations showed that higher IU was associated with lower ReHo in the left inferior frontal gyrus in the female OCD, and that lower ReHo in the right middle occipital gyrus was associated with greater obsession severity in the overall OCD sample. These findings suggest potential sex-related differences in regional neural synchrony in OCD and identify an exploratory association between IU and left inferior frontal gyrus ReHo within the female OCD subgroup. items.title: The impact of menstruation-related symptoms on women's quality of life, work productivity, and economic burden: a structured narrative review.
items.authors: Enomoto Y, Wada-Hiraike O, Nariai M, Ga H, Takai R, Furukawa M, Harada M, Hirota Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Menstruation-related disorders, including dysmenorrhoea, premenstrual syndrome (PMS)/ premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), and heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB)/ abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), are common among women of reproductive age and associated with impairments in quality of life (QOL), mental health, and daily functioning. Increasing evidence indicates that these conditions adversely affect academic and work productivity, with presenteeism constituting a major component of the economic burden. However, the existing evidence remains fragmented.

sections.heading: Materials and methods
sections.text: We conducted a structured narrative review supported by a targeted literature search of PubMed and Scopus. Studies published in English between January 2014 and December 2025 were considered if they included female individuals aged 14-59 years and examined menstruation-related symptoms in relation to QOL, work productivity, academic or occupational functioning, or economic outcomes. Because of heterogeneity in study designs, populations, and outcome measures, findings were synthesised thematically rather than quantitatively pooled.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 86 studies were used to inform the thematic synthesis. Across conditions, menstruation-related disorders were consistently associated with reduced health-related QOL, psychological distress, and impaired academic and occupational functioning. Productivity loss was observed across disorders and predominantly driven by presenteeism rather than by absenteeism. Dysmenorrhoea and PMS/PMDD were associated with both absenteeism and presenteeism, whereas HMB/AUB was strongly associated with work impairment, which is frequently mediated by anaemia-related symptoms. Psychological distress, including anxiety, depressive symptoms, emotional dysregulation, and sleep disturbance, has emerged as a key contributor to QOL impairment across age groups and regions. Lifestyle factors appeared to modify symptom severity and functional impact. Although treatment and medical consultations often improved symptoms, productivity gains were inconsistent.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This review highlights the multidimensional burden of menstruation-related disorders extending from physical symptoms to mental health and functional outcomes. The predominance of presenteeism suggested that conventional metrics based on absenteeism underestimate the true societal impact. The observed gap between symptom improvement and functional recovery underscored the need for integrated approaches that could address both clinical and psychosocial pathways.

items.title: Microbiome-driven precision psychiatry: integrating multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and personalized interventions along the gut-brain axis.
items.authors: Zhang Y, Pei C, Zhang D, Liu J.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: This scoping review maps evidence for microbiome-driven precision psychiatry in depression and anxiety.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Following JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE and PubMed Central from inception to July 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar and backward citation searching. Human primary studies were screened and charted; findings were synthesized narratively.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Of 58 identified records, 49 remained after deduplication, 35 full texts were assessed, and 28 studies were included. The evidence was predominantly observational. Taxonomic findings varied across populations, while studies of microbial functions, metabolites, multi-omics signatures, and treatment response suggested potential for biological stratification. Microbiome-targeted interventions and artificial intelligence models remain exploratory.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Microbiome-derived biomarkers and predictive models require standardized methods, independent validation, and prospective evidence of clinical utility before routine psychiatric use.

items.title: Examining child stress response, parenting and relationship-related changes associated with a dyadic mindfulness and self-compassion program.
items.authors: Lathren CR, Borelli JL, Ellsworth R, Harr E, DiMaio S, Tatera JL, Diaz V, Bluth K, Herringa RJ, Heyn SA.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Interventions that dyadically equip families with self-compassion skills represent a promising approach for addressing mental health challenges, particularly during the key transitional period of middle childhood. This study examines changes and candidate processes associated with participation in the Mindfulness and Self-Compassion for Children and Caregivers (MSC-CC) course.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Twenty-three caregiver-child dyads (Child, M _age=8.78; Caregiver, M _age=41.2) participated in MSC-CC, delivered remotely over six weekly group sessions. Pre- and post-intervention assessments included self-report measures of parenting and relational closeness outcomes during a dyadic stressor task (behavior, reflective functioning[RF], and physiology). Analyses investigated pre-post change in primary outcomes and linear mixed-effects models estimated time-related changes and baseline moderators of physiological change. Significance tests identify pre-post increases in parenting and emotion-supportive beliefs.

sections.heading: Results and discussion
sections.text: Physiologically, we detected significant decreases in child physiological arousal. Exploratory moderation analyses suggest, among others, low levels of mindfulness and high RF at baseline predict the largest reductions in child stress physiology. While uncontrolled, the MSC-CC participation was associated with increases in mindful parenting and the caregiver-child relationship and lower child physiological arousal during a dyadic challenge, most prominently in families with lower emotion-supportive beliefs at baseline. Altogether, this highlights candidate processes and moderators of efficacy to be confirmed in a fully powered randomized controlled trial.

sections.heading: Trial registration
sections.text: ClinicalTrials.gov, Self-Compassion for Children and Caregivers (SCCC), NCT05818397, registration and study start on 2023-10-16.

items.title: School-based mental health support for students with intellectual disability in the Middle East and North Africa: a 26-year scoping review.
items.authors: Alshehri M.

sections.text: Students with intellectual disability (ID) in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region face significant mental health challenges, yet the extent and nature of school-based support for them remain unclear. This scoping review mapped the English-language evidence on school-based mental health support for this population. Six sources were searched for studies published between January 2000 and May 2026. The initial search identified 255 records, of which 210 were screened, and an update search identified one further study. Six studies were included; two met all eligibility criteria and four met them in part. One study evaluated an intervention, Cognitive-Behavioral Play Therapy, and reported improved self-esteem; it was delivered in residential welfare centers rather than schools. One study reported a strong association between bullying victimization and depressive symptoms among students with mild ID. Four studies surveyed 1,037 practitioners in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates, three of them in mixed disability populations. Practitioners reported moderate and uneven preparedness in behavioral assessment, social skills training, trauma-informed practice, and mental health support, and self-efficacy and perceived school support were associated with teachers' attitudes toward supporting student mental health. No school-delivered intervention was identified, and no included study reported follow-up or a family component. Overall, the English-language evidence identified by this review is small, heterogeneous, and geographically concentrated, and few students with ID took part directly. The findings point to a need for culturally adapted school-based interventions, stronger mental health content in teacher preparation, and explicit inclusion of students with ID in regional education and mental health frameworks.

items.title: Distinct Associations of Age and CYP2D6 Genotype With Parent Venlafaxine Exposure and O-Demethylation in Japanese Psychiatric Patients.
items.authors: Ishihara Y, Sasaki T, Asahi T, Ono Y, Sugisaki T, Hiramatsu R, Kawamata Y, Sugawara N, Yasui-Furukori N.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Venlafaxine (VEN) is converted to O-desmethylvenlafaxine (ODV) mainly through CYP2D6-mediated O-demethylation. However, age-related clinical factors may also influence VEN exposure in routine practice. We examined whether age and CYP2D6 genotype show different associations with parent-drug exposure and metabolic conversion.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective therapeutic drug monitoring analysis included 78 Japanese psychiatric patients with available plasma VEN and ODV concentrations and CYP2D6 genotype data. Two prespecified outcomes were analyzed without body-weight correction: VEN concentration divided by daily dose (VEN/dose) and the ODV/VEN ratio. CYP2D6*10 and *5 were coded as reduced- and no-function alleles, respectively. Log-transformed outcomes were analyzed using regression models including age and CYP2D6 reduced/no-function allele count.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Nineteen patients (24.4%) were aged 65 years or older. Age was correlated with VEN/dose (Spearman rho = 0.295, p = 0.0086), and older patients had higher VEN/dose than younger patients (median, 0.522 vs. 0.192 [ng/mL]/[mg/day], p = 0.0127). In regression analysis, the incremental R^2 for age was numerically larger than that for CYP2D6 allele count for VEN/dose (incremental R^2, 0.058 vs. 0.026). Conversely, the ODV/VEN ratio was strongly associated with CYP2D6 allele count (standardized beta = -0.391, p < 0.001; incremental R^2 = 0.145) but not with age. Age-by-genotype interactions were not significant for either outcome.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Age appeared to be more closely related to dose-corrected parent VEN exposure, whereas CYP2D6 genotype predominantly determined the ODV/VEN metabolic ratio. The relative contribution of age should be interpreted descriptively because no formal comparison of effect sizes was performed. Separating exposure and metabolic-ratio outcomes may clarify how geriatric and pharmacogenetic factors contribute to VEN disposition.

items.title: Prevalence, knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding cognitive enhancer use in a convenience sample of university students in Syria: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Almansour S, Nasra AB, Aldakak MA, Barhoum B, Salloum J, Abidan B, Zaghbour E, Khaddam W.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Evidence on cognitive enhancer (CE) use among Middle Eastern university students remains limited, and no prior published study has characterized CE use in Syria. We assessed lifetime use, knowledge, attitudes, and use practices in a convenience sample of Syrian university students.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 707 students recruited using convenience and snowball sampling. The questionnaire used a broad intention-based definition of CE use and assessed factual knowledge, academic pressure, permissive attitudes, and use patterns. Multivariable logistic regression examined factors associated with lifetime use.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: 14.6% (103/707) reported lifetime CE use. Under the broad intention-based definition, 10.9% of the total sample reported supplement/natural-type CE use, 2.4% high-dose caffeine-product use, and 2.3% medication-type CE use; 2.0% specifically reported prescription stimulant use. Among lifetime users, use was commonly exam-related, and 29.1% reported adverse effects. In adjusted analyses, self-reported ADHD (AOR = 3.70; 95% CI: 1.18-11.55), personally knowing a CE user (AOR = 4.35; 95% CI: 2.73-6.93), and a higher permissiveness attitude score (AOR = 2.42; 95% CI: 1.72-3.41) were associated with lifetime CE use. Knowledge and academic-pressure scores were not independently associated with lifetime use.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: In this recruited sample, lifetime CE use was associated with peer exposure and permissive attitudes, whereas measured knowledge and academic pressure were not independently associated. The difference between overall CE use and medication-type use highlights the importance of distinguishing product classes when studying cognitive enhancement. Longitudinal and more representative studies are needed to clarify these associations and their generalizability.

items.title: Financial stress, mental health and help-seeking among postgraduate business students in Ghana: the moderating role of social support.
items.authors: Owusu GMY, Larry-Afutu JA, Baku AAA, Andoh-Arthur J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Higher education costs have risen significantly worldwide, creating financial pressures that adversely affect students' mental health. Postgraduate students from developing countries face acute challenges due to limited funding options. While financial stress has been linked to mental health outcomes in developed countries, studies examining these dynamics among African students remain scarce. This study examines financial stress' effects on mental health of postgraduate business students in Ghana and explores whether perceived social support moderates this relationship.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A survey was conducted with questionnaires as the means of data collection. A cross-sectional data from a sample of postgraduate students studying at a large public university in Ghana was used for the empirical analysis. The hypothesized relationships for the study were tested structurally using the Partial Least Squares (PLS) structural equation modelling technique.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Empirical results demonstrate that when students are financially stressed, they tend to have poorer mental health outcomes even with their monthly income. Social support moderated this relationship, but not significantly. Males and older students were also found to be more vulnerable to mental health problems in this study. Also, respondents' mental health help seeking behaviors did not explain their mental health outcomes.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Financial stress substantially impairs mental health among postgraduate students. Despite positive help-seeking attitudes and perceived social support, these factors did not buffer financial stress effects. Findings suggest urgent need for innovative financing schemes including grants and subsidized loans for postgraduate students, strengthened institutional mental health services, and targeted interventions addressing gender-specific vulnerabilities.

items.title: Stakeholder perspectives on the development of a school based mental health programme in Bangladesh: a qualitative needs assessment.
items.authors: Uddin MS, Sofija E, Akhter FB, Barua T, Harris P.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Bangladesh, a South Asian country where approximately one-third of the population comprises children and adolescents, has an estimated prevalence of mental disorder of 13.6% among this age group, while the treatment gap remains as high as 94.5%. A whole-school approach, grounded in the Health Promoting Schools (HPS) framework, emphasises school-community partnerships, supportive environments, curriculum integration, and enabling policy support. This study conducted a multi-level needs assessment to identify systemic gaps and capacities to inform the development of a universal school-based mental health programme (SBMHP) for adolescents.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A qualitative needs assessment was undertaken over a two-month period using sixteen focus group discussions and six key informant interviews with students (n = 48), teachers (n = 24), parents (n = 24), and mental health professionals (n = 6). Data were transcribed verbatim and analysed in NVivo 14 using a hybrid thematic approach. Deductive coding was guided by the research questions and interview guides, while inductive coding captured emergent contextual insights. Triangulation across stakeholder groups enhanced analytic rigour. The HPS framework was applied post-analysis as an interpretive lens.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A substantial mismatch emerged between adolescents' mental health promotion needs and schools' capacity to deliver coordinated preventive support. Despite stakeholder awareness, efforts were constrained by fragmented policies, limited institutional capacity, urban-centred tertiary services, and weak school-family-community collaboration. Mapping the findings onto the HPS framework indicated only partial alignment across the domains of governance, environment, curriculum, engagement, and service integration.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The study identifies structural and institutional determinants shaping adolescent mental health promotion in Bangladeshi schools and provides formative evidence to inform the future development of a culturally responsive and scalable school-based mental health promotion programme, contributing to the limited evidence base from low- and middle-income settings.

items.title: Exploring user experiences in a digital mental health app through qualitative thematic analysis.
items.authors: Varghese MA, Sharma P.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: In the recent times, the field of mental health is witnessing rolling out of digital mental health applications (apps) as a newer medium of mental health support, particularly for young adults navigating academic and life transitions. There are number of mental health apps being launched but survival and effectiveness of apps depend on various factors. As per few research studies on mental health applications, apps such as Wysa, Woebot, Talkspace, Headspace, etc. are performing well in this field. Whereas, some apps are unable to suffice the set purpose to the benefit of the users. Moreover, these apps are reaching to the people who are well versed with digital technology but leaving behind the ones unfamiliar or less familiar with the digital ecosystem. In some cases, these apps are also the first point of contact further powered by Artificial Intelligence integration. It would be of interest to understand that how these apps are being viewed by the users. As users provide important insight into the app features and effectivity to relieve their distress. Users' experiences are key to transform the mental health apps which is a viable option to narrow down the service demand and supply gap. Quality, effectivity with ethical standards are important area of current study as these apps are seen as feasible medium to combat diverse and growing mental health needs.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aims to explore user experiences, perceptions, and reported benefits and challenges associated with a digital mental health application by conducting a qualitative thematic analysis of publicly available user reviews.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This study used a user-led approach to analyze reviews (n = 3249) of the mental health app Amaha posted on the Google Play Store over a 3 years period to discover determinants for engagement and helpfulness in digital mental health. Amaha, was created in 2016 by an Indian team operating as a private entity, and offers to provide free with in app purchases mental health support to 18 and above individuals in India and with free primary information and education on mental health but advanced support comes with in-app purchase features and plans. The reported user experience was categorized and assessed into the fundamental domains of acceptability, usability, utility, and integration through the analysis of keywords in the user feedback. Along with identifying the app's main merits and shortcomings, the study also looked at the prominent features of the user types giving important information on characteristics of people accessing digital mental health care.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The analysis consisted of 3249 reviews from the year 2022 to 2025, out of which 2764 were positively rated reviews and 363 were negatively rated. The app's acceptability was demonstrated by its interactive design, entertaining exercises, and Chatbot conversational skills; its usability was emphasized by its non-judgmental nature and ease of talking. Themes including cognitive restructuring activities, easy access, and mental health enhancement demonstrated the app's value. Users' desire for the app's integrated features was highlighted by themes of privacy and confidentiality. However, affordability of the app and technical glitches were discouraging factors to using the application. Subsequent investigation identified typically four main emerging patterns in users including people communicating symptoms of depression, anxiety, stress or loneliness.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: As digital platforms are transforming mental health care, it is imperative to ensure that these tools foster genuine care and support in addition to providing scientifically sound psychological interventions, especially in low-resource settings. Knowing how users interact with Digital mental health apps is essential to understand people's expectations and nature of app usage. By offering insights that may benefit users, mental health professionals, and app developers this research advances the field of digital therapeutic solutions and brings out the trust factors and challenges in affordability of the private run mental health apps. The findings may hold important implications for universities and educational institutions exploring scalable and accessible mental health support systems for students in hybrid and post-pandemic learning environments.

items.title: Mapping neuropsychological care in pediatric epilepsy: a national survey by the Italian chapter of the international league against epilepsy (LICE).
items.authors: Zanaboni MP, Correale C, Metitieri T, Manfredi V, Offredi F, Rinaldi AB, Barco TL, Mazzone S, Bova SM, Cappelletti S.

sections.heading: Background and purpose
sections.text: Neuropsychological assessment is essential in pediatric epilepsy care, yet its implementation in clinical practice remains insufficiently characterized. This study describes neuropsychological practices across Italian pediatric epilepsy centers.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A national, cross-sectional, online survey was conducted between December 2024 and March 2025 by the Italian League Against Epilepsy. The 59-item survey assessed professional profiles, clinical practices, use of technology, and training needs. Eligible participants were psychologists and neuropsychologists involved in pediatric epilepsy care.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Twenty-three centers completed the survey (response rate 59.0%). Assessment was systematically integrated within multidisciplinary teams across diagnostic, treatment, and follow-up phases. Primary referral drivers were cognitive concerns, treatment effects, and neuropsychiatric comorbidities. Core cognitive domains were consistently assessed, though test selection varied substantially: most centers used flexible approaches, whereas 43.5% implemented standardized protocols. Screening for intellectual disability, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and learning disorders was widely applied, while severe intellectual disability evaluations relied primarily on qualitative methods. Tele-neuropsychology was used selectively for follow-up rather than primary evaluation.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This study provides the first comprehensive national mapping of pediatric epilepsy neuropsychology practices. Neuropsychological assessment is a well-established component of pediatric epilepsy care in Italy, broadly consistent with international recommendations. However, variability in organization and assessment practices highlights the need for harmonized protocols, increased resources, and specialized training. Multidisciplinary and flexible models, alongside the cautious integration of digital tools, may enhance care and improve long-term outcomes.

items.title: Mapping the neurobiological landscape linking obesity with selected psychiatric conditions: global trends and emerging hotspots.
items.authors: Liu C, Dong C, Zhou X, Shu Q, Zhang F, Cai R, Yu Q.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Obesity frequently co-occurs with a range of psychiatric conditions, creating an important global public health challenge. However, neurobiological research on these associations remains fragmented across disciplines, and a systematic bibliometric synthesis is lacking.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To map the knowledge structure, identify research hotspots, and characterize temporal trends in neurobiological research linking obesity with selected psychiatric conditions.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Relevant literature (2010-2025) was retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Following screening, 476 studies were included. Bibliometric and visualization analyses were conducted using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Scimago Graphica. A supplementary Scopus analysis assessed publication overlap and concordance in selected bibliometric indicators.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Publications surged after 2021, with the last 5 years accounting for 54.2% of the total. The United States and China had the highest publication counts. Among the 10 most productive countries, France had the highest mean annualized citations per publication. Core hotspots include neuroinflammation, the gut-brain axis, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis dysfunction, and high-fat diet.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Neuroinflammation, the gut-brain axis, and HPA-axis-related processes emerged as recurring themes. These findings highlight the need for further investigation of metabolic, immune, and neural processes in geographically diverse populations, particularly in developing regions.

items.title: Families caring for children and adolescents with rare disease: a health economic evaluation of face-to-face and online psychosocial support intervention of the randomized controlled CARE-FAM-NET study.
items.authors: Pardey N, Kreis K, Leidger A, Boettcher J, Denecke J, Soeiro Gomes S, Muntau AC, Daubmann A, Ozga AK, Zapf A, Wegscheider K, Rassenhofer M, Fegert J, Tutus D, Marschall U, Schellhammer S, Rocabado S, Krull T, Wadeck A, Schneider U, Hüttmann S, Henkel M, von der Schulenburg JM, Wiegand-Grefe S, Zeidler J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Parents caring for children with rare diseases often experience a reduced Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL). This study addresses the growing need for therapeutic support by evaluating two innovative forms of care: CARE-FAM (CF) and a web-based program (WEP) WEP-CARE (WC). CF is a psychodynamic-psychosocial intervention with eight sessions per family over six months, aiming to improve mental health, HRQoL, and satisfaction of all family members. WC is an online intervention leveraging cognitive-behavioral writing therapy principles to achieve the same objectives. The aim of this study was to evaluate the incremental cost per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained for CF, WC and their combination (CF + WC) compared with the control group (CG), on a per-parent basis, over an 18-month time horizon from the German statutory health insurance (SHI) payer perspective.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Children Affected by Rare disease and Their Families - Research Network (CARE-FAM-Net) is a 2 × 2 factorial, multicenter randomized controlled study conducted across 17 psychiatric hospitals in Germany with three intervention groups (CF, WC, CF + WC) and a control group. Cost evaluations utilized claims data from seven SHI funds, reflecting the SHI payer perspective, while QALYs were calculated using the EQ-5D-3 L score at four points over an 18-month time horizon. The unit of analysis was the individual parent, therefore all costs and QALYs were estimated on a per-parent basis. The primary analysis used the intention-to-treat statutory health insurance (ITT-SHI) population. Missing data were addressed through multiple imputation by chained equations with predictive mean matching, generating 20 imputed datasets that were combined using Rubin's rules. Within-family correlation was accounted for in the statistical analyses. Numerical incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were reported where appropriate, and non-parametric family-cluster bootstrapping was performed to estimate statistical uncertainty. The sensitivity analysis used a restricted population. Costs and QALYs were discounted at a rate of 3%.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The primary ITT-SHI analysis included 653 participants, with a mean age of 39.4 years (SD 7.2), and 396 (60.6%) were female. Unadjusted mean annual discounted costs per parent were €4476 (SE €631) for CG, €3539 (SE €755) for CF, €3970 (SE €1249) for WC and €5518 (SE €1850) for CF + WC. Unadjusted mean annual discounted QALYs per parent were 0.9144 (SE 0.0079) for CG, 0.9215 (SE 0.0097) for CF, 0.9287 (SE 0.0074) for WC and 0.9313 (SE 0.0075) for CF + WC. Based on the incremental mean costs and baseline-adjusted QALY differences, CF and WC dominated CG, whereas CF + WC had an ICER of €109,371 per QALY gained. However, none of the between-group differences in costs or baseline-adjusted QALYs were statistically significant. At a willingness-to-pay (WTP) of €50,000 per QALY, the probabilities of cost-effectiveness in pairwise comparisons with CG were 84.2% for CF, 79.9% for WC, and 43.0% for CF + WC. When all strategies were compared simultaneously, WC had the highest probability of being the most cost-effective strategy (48.2%), followed by CF (37.6%), CF + WC (10.4%) and CG (3.8%). The sensitivity analysis yielded comparable results for CF and WC, whereas CF + WC also dominated CG. Leave-one-out analyses demonstrated sensitivity to individual extreme cost observations.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: In the primary analysis, CF and WC were associated with lower mean costs and positive baseline-adjusted QALY differences relative to CG, whereas CF + WC was associated with higher mean costs and a positive baseline-adjusted QALY difference. None of the differences in costs or baseline-adjusted QALYs were statistically significant. The sensitivity analysis yielded broadly comparable findings for CF and WC, whereas results differed for CF + WC. Given the study limitations, particularly the relatively small sample size, the current evidence is insufficient to support a definitive recommendation for implementation into routine care from a health economic perspective.

sections.heading: Trial registration
sections.text: The study was registered at 18th December 2018 at the German clinical trials register (Deutsches Register Klinischer Studien, DRKS, nr: DRKS00015859).

items.title: Meta Mesh Ontology for Cross-Domain Mental Health Knowledge Integration: Development and Evaluation Study.
items.authors: Blitz R, Richter M, Kerber A, Leenings R, Thun S, Opel N.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Psychiatric diagnostic practice faces persistent challenges in adequately capturing the complexity, heterogeneity, and dynamic nature of mental disorders. Conventional categorical classification systems such as the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) and the International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision (ICD-11) rely on rigid symptom-based criteria that often fail to represent multifactorial etiologies, dimensional symptom profiles, and high rates of comorbidity. Although dimensional models, domain-specific ontologies, and alternative taxonomies have been developed to address these limitations, they are typically applied in isolation, resulting in fragmented knowledge representations and limited interoperability. This lack of semantic integration hampers data harmonization and cross-domain analysis.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: The objective of this work is to develop and present the Meta Mesh Ontology (MMO) and its Core Domain Framework (CDF) as an integrative approach for mapping heterogeneous psychiatric knowledge bases and evaluating ontology structure, logical consistency, and specified retrieval and inference behavior.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We designed a modular ontology architecture grounded in the Basic Formal Ontology to ensure structural and semantic consistency across biological, psychological, and social domains. Existing psychiatric frameworks and ontologies-including dimensional models, diagnostic taxonomies, and socioenvironmental knowledge systems-were systematically analyzed and represented through domain modules using a documented alignment and mapping procedure. The MMO was implemented using formal semantic web standards, including the Web Ontology Language and the Resource Description Framework (RDF), and aligned with established biomedical ontologies and informatics standards to support explicit mappings and modular extensions across domains. Evaluation used 2 MMO and CDF metric sets and 10 module metric sets to quantify ontology size, semantic alignments, external integration, and dataset readiness. We also assessed Web Ontology Language 2 Description Logic (OWL 2 DL) conformance, logical consistency, and 11 competency questions (including 1 entailment test) and 4 negative controls, in an outpatient scenario with 50 variables.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The MMO provides a shared semantic framework for representing links among heterogeneous psychiatric knowledge sources. Its modular design allows domain-specific subontologies to be incorporated under a common architecture. MMO and CDF comprised 2238 triples, 208 classes, 28 properties, 3 individuals, and 103 alignments (100 external) across 5 frameworks. The 10 modules added 967 triples and 171 alignments (116 external), with 21 integrations and complete label coverage (54/54 resources). The ontology resources conformed to OWL 2 DL; HermiT (Information Systems Group) detected no logical inconsistency, and all 11 competency questions and 4 negative controls produced the expected results. All 50 variables were linked to at least 1 CDF anchor, and 47 had an explicit Simple Knowledge Organization System (SKOS) mapping.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The MMO provides a modular foundation for representing links among diverse psychiatric knowledge systems and data modalities. The current evaluation characterizes its structure, mappings, and behavior in the specified tests. Further research should assess mapping validity, governed clinical data, operational performance, and clinical utility.

items.title: Direct pathways from anthropomorphism to self-disclosure in artificial intelligence Chatbot use: a mixed-methods multi-study investigation.
items.authors: Rahman W.

sections.text: Anthropomorphic design is widely assumed to shape self-disclosure and emotional dependence by first cultivating felt empathy and trust, and the safety measures platforms deploy, such as labelling and disclosure of artificial origin, target those perceptions. Across a twelve-country survey, forty-seven interviews, and three experiments, this research tests that mediation model and identifies the route that carries the behavioural effect. A twelve-country survey ( N  = 1480) found empathy and trust negligibly related to disclosure and dependence at the trait level. Two experiments ( N  = 390 and N  = 300) produced strong direct effects of an anthropomorphic agent, with the anthropomorphic agent roughly tripling the odds of behavioural disclosure (63% versus 35% under a matched neutral prompt), while the indirect effects through empathy and trust received no support. Study 5 ( N  = 300) measured competing mediators and provided the most defensible interim account of the mechanism: only perceived anonymity and reduced evaluation apprehension carried the effect on disclosure, locating the process in online disinhibition rather than felt relational warmth. Forty-seven interviews surfaced clinically salient disclosure, including suicidal ideation revealed to a chatbot and to no person. Because the consequences of anthropomorphic design travel through the lowered social risk of the medium, safeguards that recalibrate how users perceive an agent may leave disclosure and dependence largely untouched.

Because the consequences of anthropomorphic design travel through the lowered social risk of the medium, safeguards that recalibrate how users perceive an agent may leave disclosure and dependence largely untouched.

items.title: Latent profiles of health empowerment and associated factors among older adults hospitalised with stroke: a single-centre cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Xin Q, Mao Y, Lei Y, Li X, Shan Y, Meng L.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: This study aims to explore the health empowerment of elderly ischemic stroke patients in China and analyze its associated factors.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Ischemic stroke patients hospitalized in the Department of Neurology and Rehabilitation of a tertiary hospital in Daqing from June 2025 to March 2026 were the research subjects.The general information questionnaire, the Health Empowerment Nursing Evaluation Scale for stroke patients, the electronic health literacy scale, the chronic disease resource utilization scale, the simplified version of the disease perception scale, the family APGAR questionnaire, and the coping style scale were used to investigate.The potential profile analysis was used to explore the potential subtypes of health empowerment in ischemic stroke patients, and multivariate logistic regression was used to analyze the associated factors of different types of health empowerment.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Health empowerment in elderly ischemic stroke patients can be divided into three subtypes: low health empowerment - low information access group (53.39%), moderate health empowerment - balanced support group (8.21%), and high health empowerment - high stress coping group (38.39%). Multiple logistic regression showed that electronic health literacy, disease perception, and family care were independently correlated with patients' health empowerment levels (all P < 0.05); However, the utilization of chronic disease resources and coping strategies did not have independent predictive effects in multiple logistic regression (P > 0.05), nor did they include significant influencing factors.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: There is a heterogeneity in the level of health empowerment of elderly ischemic stroke patients, and healthcare professionals should take targeted measures to improve their health empowerment level and promote their physical and mental health.

items.title: Understanding the needs and frustrations in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a qualitative interview study.
items.authors: Sykorova K, Pavel N, Mathew A, Johnsen MB, Ullevoldsæter Lystad J, Bull HC, Gazerani P, Kvammen MF, Hong-Gu H, Jacoby J, Pikkarainen MA.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Scoliosis is a common term used for a group of conditions that involve abnormal curvature and rotation of the spine, thorax, and trunk. If untreated, scoliosis may lead to severe trunk deformities, which consequently limit physical function, exercise capacity, general well-being, ability to work, and the mental health of affected individuals. Little is known about how adolescents with Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) and their caregivers cope with scoliosis and what kind of needs, frustrations, and difficulties they experience during treatment.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: This study aimed to explore the difficulties, needs, and frustrations experienced by adolescents with AIS and their caregivers.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: An exploratory qualitative design was adopted. A total of 17 participants were recruited through purposive sampling with the aid of user organizations and hospitals in Norway from April to August in 2023. A total of five audio-recorded, semi-structured focus group interviews were conducted, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using thematic analysis. The discussions focused on the needs, frustrations, and challenges of adolescents with AIS and their caregivers.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: This study explored the needs for improvement in health care services related to AIS in Norway, from the perspectives of adolescents and caregivers. Participants reported a lack of communication and information surrounding AIS diagnosis, forcing them to actively seek help. Gaps were also reported, in post-operative follow-up care and conservative treatment of scoliosis, where adolescents with AIS feel overlooked and alone in their recovery and physiotherapy. Participants voiced frustrations, including the psychosocial impact of the condition which affects school attendance due to back pain and absence from activities, leading to feelings of isolation.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The study identified significant gaps in Norway's AIS health care services that could be addressed with digital solutions. Adolescents with AIS and caregivers reported inadequate communication, poor post-operative care, and struggles with conservative treatment.

items.title: Validation of the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS) in Diné bizaad (Navajo): randomized comparison of a community translation versus a forward translation.
items.authors: Dutta T, Begay TII, Williams J, Zimet G, Radtke J, Dickinson S, Agley J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS) is a 12-item psychometric instrument that assesses perceived social support (PSS) with a well-established three-factor structure: family, friends, and significant others. Having a way to measure PSS is important because PSS is only moderately correlated to objective social support. As one of the most widely used and cited measures of PSS, the MSPSS has been translated from English into dozens of languages. However, some authors have been critical of some MSPSS translation and validation studies, particularly when the translation processes do not conduct confirmatory factor analyses or report different numbers of factors when validating the translated instrument. Previously, members of our research team conducted a community-engaged study to develop a culturally-informed translation of the MSPSS into Diné bizaad (Navajo). This study aimed to examine the factor structure and internal reliability of the community-based translation of the MSPSS and a control condition (a basic forward translation) and to provide a descriptive comparison of the results by study arm.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a randomized controlled trial with 1:1 blinded allocation to compare the community-engaged translation of the MSPSS to a control condition. Two-hundred bilingual Navajo/English speakers in La Plata County, CO were randomly assigned to complete one of the two instruments (n = 100 per study arm). We conducted confirmatory factor analysis on each arm separately, using a robust MLR estimator with listwise deletion to compute both absolute and incremental fit indices, and computed Cronbach's alpha for reliability of each subscale.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Both translations adequately fit the three-factor structure. While we did not conduct direct statistical comparisons, descriptive comparisons indicated that the forward translation showed better model fit in terms of incremental indices as well as one of the absolute fit indices (SRMR), while the community translation showed two better absolute fit indices (RMSEA and χ^2/df ratio). Subscale internal consistency ranged from.72 to.78 for the community translation and from.87 to.89 for the forward translation.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Contrary to our expectations, the fit indices were mixed and did not clearly support one particular translation. We discuss potential reasons for this finding and implications thereof.

items.title: Communicating with diverse populations before, during and after Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) events: systematic literature review.
items.authors: Brooks SK, Rogers MB, Pearce JM.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) events can have substantial impacts on affected individuals and communities. Effective communication is an essential component of preparedness and response in the context of CBRN events. While there is a wealth of literature on communicating effectively with the general public during such events, less is known about the communication needs of diverse populations who may be disproportionately affected during CBRN incidents. This review aimed to examine the available evidence regarding the need for and impacts of tailored communication strategies for diverse populations across the preparedness, response, and recovery phases of a CBRN event.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this PRISMA-based systematic review, we searched eight electronic databases for literature on the communication needs of diverse populations during CBRN events and hand-searched the reference lists of included studies and of relevant websites. Data were extracted and synthesised using thematic analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Database searches yielded 5,354 citations and 34 were included in the review. Studies considering pre-incident communication needs of diverse populations suggest that knowledge of and preparedness for CBRN events is low across the groups studied. Most studies focused on communication/information needs of diverse populations during CBRN incidents. Within this response space we identified: different drivers for protective behaviours during a CBRN event; three main information needs (basic information about the incident, CBRN health risk information, and protection information); and three key needs relating to the method of communication (trusted sources, different modes and mediums of communication, and inclusive/accessible communication) during CBRN events. We also identified challenges faced by at-risk groups during mass casualty management, which underscored the need for tailored communication. Ten studies considered post-incident needs, with data indicating the importance of ongoing support and information, information on potential mental health effects, and communication relating to ongoing monitoring and research.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This review highlighted important commonalities in information needs underscoring that transparent, consistent, factually correct information from trusted sources about health risks and protective behaviours is required for everyone irrespective of background. However, it also revealed important differences in health beliefs and concerns; risk perceptions; and trusted information sources, necessitating tailoring context-sensitive messages for diverse populations. Incorporating these considerations into preparedness and response planning for CBRN events is crucial for improving public understanding and facilitating appropriate response behaviours.

items.title: Toxic leadership and employee health: exploring psychosocial stress pathways in organizational settings.
items.authors: Altassan MA.

sections.text: Toxic leadership poses a profound threat to employee well-being, particularly within high-context, collectivist cultures where hierarchical norms often suppress resistance. Despite growing interest globally, its psychosocial effects in Middle Eastern organizational settings remain underexplored. This qualitative study examines how toxic leadership affects the health and well-being of employees working in healthcare, business, and education organizations in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, with particular attention to lived experiences and culturally specific coping strategies. Using an interpretivist qualitative design, semi-structured interviews were conducted in English with 42 employees from healthcare (n = 10), business (n = 12), and education (n = 20) organizations in Jeddah. Participants were purposively selected based on self-reported experience of or direct observation of recurrent harmful supervisory behaviors. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis, resulting in seven overarching themes: (1) Silent Suffering, employees experience fear, suppression, and emotional paralysis; (2) Cultural Rationalization of Abuse, submission and religious values normalize toxicity; (3) Emotional and Mental Drain, including anxiety, burnout, and psychosomatic symptoms; (4) Coping Strategies and Resistance, faith, peer support, and avoidance tactics; (5) Leadership as Untouchable Power, reinforced by favoritism and wasta; (6) Organizational Silence and HR Inaction, ineffective grievance mechanisms and distrust; and (7) Normalization and Identity Conflict, ethical erosion and emotional numbness. Findings enrich the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) and Conservation of Resources (COR) models by contextualizing them within Saudi cultural dynamics. This study underscores the urgency for culturally aligned leadership development, mental health integration, and anti-toxic policy frameworks in the Saudi workplace.

items.title: A blood aging clock defines disease-induced deviation from healthy molecular aging.
items.authors: Li H, Liu S, Zhou Z, Lu Q, Wang G, Zhu Z, Li X.

sections.text: Aging shapes disease susceptibility and recovery, yet it remains unclear whether disease-induced molecular perturbations can be quantitatively mapped onto healthy aging trajectories. Here, we integrated 10 753 whole-blood transcriptomic profiles from 23 cohorts and developed a blood aging predictor (BAP) using 5808 healthy individuals to define a reference trajectory of blood molecular aging. Applying BAP to COVID-19 revealed marked transcriptomic age acceleration (AgeAccel), with patients showing an average AgeAccel of 9.34 years after cohort-specific baseline correction. This aging-referenced deviation occurred across age groups and was associated with interferon signaling, immune-inflammatory activation, cytokine and neutrophil-related programs, DNA damage responses, proteostasis stress, and impaired cellular quality-control pathways. Longitudinal analysis showed that AgeAccel increased during acute infection but declined during recovery, indicating a potentially reversible aging-like molecular state at the cohort level rather than irreversible aging. Extension to sepsis, influenza, and major depressive disorder further demonstrated that elevated AgeAccel captures disease-associated molecular burden across distinct pathological contexts. Together, our study redefines transcriptomic AgeAccel as an interpretable measure of disease-induced deviation from healthy molecular homeostasis and provides a quantitative framework for assessing systemic disease burden and recovery dynamics from peripheral blood transcriptomes.

items.title: Diagnostic Challenge of Primary Psychiatric Catatonia Versus Seronegative Autoimmune Encephalitis in Pediatrics: A Case Report.
items.authors: Ohabuenyi S, Kunta C, Udom K, Bhagi N, Ebere-Bank D.

sections.text: Catatonia in adolescents presents a diagnostic challenge when autoimmune and psychiatric etiologies overlap. We describe a 16-year-old male with recurrent severe catatonia, complete mutism, and functional decline over four months. Despite a comprehensive negative autoimmune workup, inflammatory markers (elevated interleukin-2 receptor) and clinical features suggested seronegative autoimmune encephalitis. The patient required high-dose lorazepam (18 milligrams per day) and received empiric immunotherapy with intravenous immunoglobulin and corticosteroids, followed by enrollment in a specialized electroconvulsive therapy program. He demonstrated substantial improvement with the return of bilingual speech and social interaction. This case illustrates the importance of maintaining a broad differential diagnosis in adolescent catatonia and considering empiric immunotherapy when clinical suspicion for autoimmune etiology remains high despite negative antibody testing.

items.title: The association of cognitive behavioral intervention with caregiver burden and quality of life among family caregivers of cancer recurrence patients.
items.authors: Zhang Z, Zhou H, Guo X, Zheng B.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to evaluate the immediate and 3-month follow-up associations of cognitive behavioral intervention (CBI) on caregiver burden and quality of life (QOL) among family caregivers of patients with recurrent cancer.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A quasi-experimental study was conducted among 87 family caregivers of patients with recurrent cancer who completed the study at a tertiary hospital in China. Participants were recruited from two inpatient wards within the same oncology department, with one ward assigned to the intervention arm (n=43) and the other to the control arm (n=44). The intervention group received an 8-week structured CBI alongside routine care, while the control group received routine care alone. Outcomes were measured using the Zarit Burden Interview (ZBI) and the World Health Organization Quality of Life-BREF-Chinese Version (WHOQOL-BREF-CV), which were administered at baseline (T_0), immediately post-intervention (T_1), and 3-month post-intervention follow-up (T_2).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Compared with the control group, the intervention group showed significant reductions in total caregiver burden at both T_1 (MD = -8.27, 95% CI: -10.39 to -6.16; d  = -1.66) and T_2 (MD = -4.66, 95% CI: -6.92 to -2.40; d  = -0.88). Significant improvements were also observed in overall QOL at T_1 (MD = 3.39, 95% CI: 1.46 to 5.32; d  = 0.75) and T_2 (MD = 3.91, 95% CI: 1.83 to 5.99; d  = 0.80), as well as in the physical domain at T_1 and T_2, and in the psychological domain at T_1. However, the psychological-domain difference at T_2 was less robust in post hoc multiplicity-adjusted sensitivity analyses. However, between-group differences in the social relationships and environmental domains were not statistically significant at T_2 ( p > 0.05). The control group showed no significant longitudinal changes in caregiver burden; however, significant within-group fluctuations were observed in several QOL domains over time.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The findings suggest that CBI may be associated with reduced caregiver burden and improved QOL among family caregivers of patients with recurrent cancer over the immediate and 3-month follow-up period. Further large-scale, multi-center studies with extended follow-up are recommended to confirm the sustainability of these effects and the generalizability of the intervention.

items.title: Toward a population-level public health approach to support families living under continuous traumatic stress.
items.authors: Gewirtz AH, Keleynikov M, Eliash-Fizik H, Lewis N, Gale J, Itzhaky-Wruble S, Hoffnung-Assouline A, Viner A.

sections.text: Since October 2023, families across Israel have been living under conditions of continuous traumatic stress (CTS): ongoing, unresolved threat due to repeated rounds of regional conflict. Demand for mental health support has far outstripped the capacity of clinician-delivered services, leaving many families without evidence-based help. This community case study describes the development and early implementation of ADAPT-Israel. To our knowledge, this is likely to be the first population-level, parenting-centered public health approach designed for families living under CTS. The initiative uses a tiered model to provide parenting support across layers of care: (i) a universal layer of brief, trauma-informed public health messages and a self-directed, interactive online parenting program (with an optional AI avatar guide); (ii) a selective layer of facilitator-delivered ADAPT groups for live higher-risk families, beginning with families of long-serving military reservists; and (iii) an indicated layer of individual telehealth support for families experiencing clinical levels of difficulty. The approach adapts Adaptive Parenting Tools/ADAPT, an evidence-based program grounded in Social Interaction Learning theory and validated in a different context - for military families in the United States across three randomized controlled trials with nearly 1,000 military families. We describe the rationale, the methodology used to develop each tier, and early implementation experience. Feasibility and acceptability indicators from initial pilot groups are promising, including high group completion and positive participant reports of improved parenting and family relationships, though these are small-sample, self-report, early-stage findings rather than effectiveness evidence. items.title: Kinesiophobia following ACL reconstruction: a qualitative netnographic study of lived experiences shared on Reddit.
items.authors: Kahve Y, Darben Azarsiz Y, Aydin S, Aydin T, Gurhan U, Civan Kahve A.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Kinesiophobia, broadly defined as fear of movement and vulnerability to (re)injury, is one of the most significant psychological barriers to functional recovery following anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction, yet its everyday, lived texture is not fully captured by structured psychometric instruments. Orthopedic clinicians frequently observe that patients who have achieved objective surgical and functional recovery nonetheless remain reluctant to resume movement. This study aimed to explore this phenomenon in patients' own words.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a qualitative netnographic study of 50 first-person Reddit narratives shared by individuals with ACL injury, spanning the rehabilitation trajectory from preoperative anxiety to chronic post-return instability. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis by an interdisciplinary team of orthopedic surgeons and psychiatrists.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Three interconnected themes emerged. First, a progressive loss of trust in the injured body, in which normal postoperative sensations were hypervigilantly monitored and catastrophically reinterpreted as signs of graft failure, persisting even after objective strength testing and medical clearance. Second, fear-driven disruption of functional identity and future planning, in which reinjury fear extended beyond the knee to threaten occupational continuity, financial security, and physical self-concept. Third, persistent uncertainty and compulsive reassurance-seeking, fueled by inconsistent rehabilitation guidance and unfavorable social comparison with peers' recovery timelines on social media.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Psychological readiness for return to activity appears to be shaped by an interacting network of bodily, identity-related, and informational factors that extend beyond fear of reinjury as traditionally measured. Incorporating expectation management, structured reassurance, and psychologically informed communication into postoperative care protocols may benefit orthopedic and rehabilitation teams. Naturally occurring online narratives may serve as an ecologically valid source of insight into the psychological dimensions of ACL recovery, complementing structured psychometric assessment.

items.title: University physical education course experience and resilience-based psychological recovery capacity among students in Chinese higher education: indirect associations through emotion regulation, exercise self-efficacy, and peer connectedness.
items.authors: Yang W, Meng L.

sections.text: University students face increasing psychological pressure, yet formal mental health services often remain limited in reach and depend on active help-seeking. This study examines university physical education (PE) as an educational context whose perceived qualities may be associated with psychological resources relevant to adaptation under stress. Using cross-sectional survey data from 831 Chinese college students, we examined whether perceived PE course experience was associated with resilience-based psychological recovery capacity and whether this association was indirectly linked through emotion regulation, exercise self-efficacy, and peer connectedness. The retained measurement specification represented PE course experience as a second-order construct comprising teacher support, mastery climate, embodied engagement, emotional release, and peer interaction. Structural equation modeling indicated that PE course experience was positively associated with resilience-based psychological recovery capacity and with all three proposed indirect-linking variables. Bootstrapping results supported significant indirect associations through emotion regulation, exercise self-efficacy, and peer connectedness, with exercise self-efficacy showing the largest estimated indirect association. The association remained significant after controlling for perceived stress and extracurricular exercise frequency. These findings link perceived PE course qualities with resilience-based adaptive capacity, conditional on the measured covariates. They do not isolate curriculum effects from physical-activity exposure. Because the design is cross-sectional, the findings should be interpreted as theoretically grounded associations rather than causal effects.
