items.title: Psychiatric education in medical training: a scoping review of curricular innovations, teaching strategies, and assessment methods.
items.authors: Aqtam I, Mansor K, Shouli M.
items.journal: International journal of mental health systems

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Mental disorders contribute substantially to global disease burden, yet persistent deficiencies remain in medical trainees' readiness to identify, diagnose, and treat patients with mental health conditions. Main barriers include stigma, outdated curricula, insufficient clinical practice, and regional differences in mental health services.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: This scoping review systematically mapped existing research on educational innovations, learning approaches, and evaluation instruments in psychiatric education for medical learners (2015-2026), with formal quality appraisal using a JBI-adapted tool.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, and Scopus. The PCC model guided eligibility. Two reviewers independently selected articles and extracted data. A ten-item JBI-adapted quality appraisal checklist was applied to all included studies. The evidence base comprised 34 primary empirical studies (77.3%) and 10 secondary or contextual sources (22.7%).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Of 3,682 articles identified, 44 met inclusion criteria 34 primary empirical studies (77.3%) and 10 secondary sources (22.7%). Most originated from the United States (54.5%), focusing on undergraduate learners (88.6%). Quality appraisal revealed only 34.1% used validated measures, 20.5% included follow-up, and 18.2% fully met control group criteria. Thematic analysis identified five themes: curricular innovations, educational approaches, assessment methods, Kirkpatrick-classified outcomes, and implementation barriers/facilitators. While all 44 reported Level 1 and Level 2 outcomes, measured in primary studies and discussed in secondary sources, no studies measured Level 3 behavioral change or Level 4 patient outcomes.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The absence of Level 3 and Level 4 evidence represents a major limitation and priority for future research; it does not imply health systems cannot invest in psychiatric education, but that the evidence base has not yet demonstrated translation to improved clinical behaviors or patient outcomes. Future research should prioritize longitudinal and system-level evaluation with validated behavioral and patient-level outcome measures.

items.title: Effectiveness of self-administered acupressure intervention in managing constipation of adult psychiatric out-patient - a pilot study.
items.authors: Wong WK, Wong OYJ, Law CC, Wong KL, Man YL, Chun TS, Leong SL, Lee WM, Chan A, Yan NK, Yu Tam P.
items.journal: International journal of nursing studies advances

sections.heading: Aims
sections.text: To evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of a nurse-delivered, self-administered acupressure protocol for psychiatric outpatients with constipation; to examine preliminary effects on constipation severity and constipation-related quality of life; and to document changes in laxative use and psychotropic medication during the intervention.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Constipation is common among psychiatric patients receiving second-generation antipsychotics. Pharmacological treatments may cause adverse effects, while existing non-pharmacological approaches are resource intensive. A safe, low-cost, patient-centred, self-administered intervention is needed.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: This pilot study used a single-group pretest-posttest design with assessments at baseline and immediately post-intervention. Convenience sampling recruited Hong Kong Chinese psychiatric outpatients aged 18-60 years who met Rome IV criteria for constipation and were clinically stable.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Participants attended a three-hour home training session, delivered by a Community Psychiatric Nurse, on a self-administered acupressure protocol, followed by a 10-day home practice period. Feasibility was assessed by adherence. Constipation severity was measured with the Chinese Constipation Assessment Scale, and constipation-related quality of life with the Chinese Patient Assessment of Constipation Quality of Life questionnaire. Laxative use and psychotropic regimens were recorded.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Seventy-two participants were recruited. Adherence to the 10-day protocol was 100%. Constipation Assessment Scale scores decreased by 2.28 points, while quality-of-life scores improved by 17.01 points. Reduced laxative reliance was observed without changes in psychotropic regimens.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Nurse-delivered training in self-administered acupressure appears feasible, acceptable, and low-cost for managing constipation in psychiatric outpatients, with promising improvements in symptoms and quality of life.

items.title: Attitude Toward Persons With Mental Illness in Bangladesh: Scale Validation and Status Assessment.
items.authors: Arafat SMY, Hossain S, Islam MK, Huq M, Mouri FK, Ahmed S, Khan ST, Mali B, Hossain MS.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Stigma toward persons with mental illness remains a major barrier to mental health care. No validated Bangla instrument is available to assess attitudes toward persons with mental illness in Bangladesh.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to adapt and validate the culturally adapted Bangla version of the Attitudes Toward Persons with Mental Illness (APMI) scale and to assess attitudes among undergraduate medical students and Islamic religious leaders in Bangladesh.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A psychometric validation study was conducted from July 2025 to June 2026 among 489 participants (249 medical students and 240 Imams). The original 16-item APMI scale was translated and culturally adapted following standard guidelines. The sample was independently divided into exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 245) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 244) subsamples. EFA used polychoric correlations, minimum residual extraction, oblimin rotation, and parallel analysis. CFA compared one- and two-factor models using the WLSMV estimator. Reliability, measurement invariance, group differences, and multivariable associations were also evaluated.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: EFA supported a two-factor structure comprising Fear/Social Avoidance and Interpersonal Acceptance. The correlated two-factor CFA model showed substantially better fit than the one-factor model (scaled CFI = 0.967, TLI = 0.956, RMSEA = 0.071, 90% CI 0.049-0.092, SRMR = 0.046). Ordinal alpha was 0.83 and 0.78. Measurement invariance was supported at the configural, partial metric, and partial threshold/scalar levels. Medical students had lower scores than Imams. After adjustment, the difference remained significant ( β = 5.02, 95% CI 2.89-7.15; p < 0.001).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The 10-item culturally adapted Bangla APMI scale demonstrates acceptable structural validity and internal consistency for assessing attitudes toward persons with mental illness for Bangla-speaking populations.

items.title: Who benefits from long-term care insurance? Heterogeneous effects among spousal and adult-child caregivers in China.
items.authors: Qiu Y, Ohinata A.

sections.text: China's 2016 long-term care insurance (LTCI) pilots represent one of the world's largest social-care policy experiments. Using the five waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) from 2011 to 2020, we examine how access to LTCI affects the physical and mental health of informal caregivers. We distinguish between spousal caregivers and adult-child caregivers. The latter provide nearly half of all informal care yet have received little attention in the literature. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design, we find that LTCI reduces physical pain for both groups of caregivers, although its effects on their mental health are limited. Our findings highlight the uneven health benefits of social-care reform and underscore the need for policies that provide stronger mental health support for caregivers in ageing societies.

items.title: Markers of blood-brain barrier and intestinal mucosal barrier in insomnia disorder: an observational study linking wake-promoting neurotransmitters to sleep efficiency.
items.authors: Lin J, Cai Y, Yang X, Liu Y, Shi X, Xu Y, Pan J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The present study aimed to investigate the alterations in wake-promoting neurotransmitters (histamine and orexin-A) and markers of blood-brain barrier and intestinal mucosal barrier including zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1), claudin-5, zonulin, and S100 calcium-binding protein B (S100β) in insomnia disorder (ID). Additionally, we examined the correlations between these neurotransmitters and barrier markers, and explored their combined associations with sleep parameters.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This study enrolled 54 ID patients and 45 healthy controls. The demographic and clinical characteristics of all participants were investigated, and participants underwent overnight polysomnography. Serum levels of wake-promoting neurotransmitters and barrier markers were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Spearman's correlation analysis was conducted to explore the associations between these serum biomarkers and sleep parameters, as well as between the neurotransmitters and barrier markers. Furthermore, mediation analysis was performed to examine whether barrier markers mediated the relationship between wake-promoting neurotransmitters and sleep parameters.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Levels of peripheral wake-promoting neurotransmitters (histamine and orexin-A) and barrier markers (zonulin, S100β, ZO-1, and claudin-5) were elevated in the ID group (all p < 0.001). Additionally, sleep efficiency was positively correlated with histamine levels (r = 0.57), negatively correlated with orexin-A levels (r = -0.62), and positively correlated with ZO-1 levels (r = 0.56) in ID patients. Moreover, histamine levels showed positive correlations with claudin-5 (r = 0.37) and ZO-1 (r = 0.31), and a negative correlation with S100β (r = -0.33). Additionally, orexin-A was negatively correlated with claudin-5 levels (r = -0.46). Furthermore, ZO-1 showed a statistical mediation effect in the associations between histamine and sleep efficiency (p = 0.006) as well as between orexin-A and sleep efficiency (p = 0.012), consistent with a potential indirect pathway.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This study observed dysregulation of peripheral wake-promoting neurotransmitters along with markers of blood-brain barrier and intestinal mucosal barrier in ID patients. Notably, ZO-1 showed a statistical mediation effect in the associations between these neurotransmitters and sleep efficiency, though causality cannot be inferred from the cross-sectional design. These clinical findings provide preliminary insights into the molecular features associated with ID and may inform directions for future mechanistic research. Further studies are needed to fully elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

items.title: 'Taking care of your mind': participatory research to identify priorities and co-design wellbeing resources with the Muslim community following COVID-19.
items.authors: Douglass CH, Orozco AL, Unal R, Hassan S, Shahwar D, Grindlay C, Geereh S, Mah V, Hellard M, Kirwan A, Pedrana A.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Throughout COVID-19, public health responses lacked engagement with multicultural communities. Collaborating with multicultural communities is essential to understand priorities and create culturally appropriate solutions. Our participatory study aimed to identify the public health priorities of the Muslim community, explore potential solutions, develop resources and monitor their uptake.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In 2022, we formed a research-community partnership with the Burnet Institute, Islamic Museum of Australia, Australian Multicultural Foundation and Your Community Health. Together, we co-developed a cross-sectional survey to identify the priorities of a Muslim community in Melbourne, Australia following the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants (n = 57) were recruited through the networks of three bilingual project officers and Preston Mosque. Participants reported what they needed to feel safe, supported and healthy, ranking 15 items. Through open-ended responses, participants could elaborate on their support needs. We then conducted two participatory and interactive workshops with eight Muslim community members to explore potential solutions to identified needs. Data were synthesised in Miro and validated through partner meetings. Together, we drew on results to develop a series of resources. We monitored resource uptake through partner interviews (n = 4), a document review and descriptive statistics.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Survey results indicated that participants most needed jobs (60%), mental health support (43%) and education (40%) to feel safe, supported and healthy after the pandemic. In open-text responses, participants identified they wanted improved access to psychological wellbeing support for themselves, their families and communities. Workshop participants recommended encouraging mental health conversations, providing support through mosques and raising awareness about mental health support online. Subsequently, we co-designed a facilitator guide to support Muslim community members to lead conversations about mental health. We also developed five videos to promote mental health awareness among the Muslim community. We identified that partners used the facilitator guide in three community workshops, referred 20 people to Mental Health First Aid Training and began offering counselling from Preston Mosque. Videos received > 17,000 YouTube views.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Our findings identified the importance of accessible mental health support among the Muslim community following COVID-19. Our partnership enabled the co-design and sharing of culturally safe mental health resources through preferred community channels.

sections.heading: Trial registration
sections.text: Not applicable.

items.title: Overall, emotional and social loneliness and their associated factors: a large-scale cross-sectional study of young and middle-aged adults in Germany.
items.authors: Kleinschlömer P, Ludwig-Walz H, Diabaté S, Bujard M.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Loneliness is increasingly recognized as a major public health concern, yet little is known about the distinct patterns and associated factors of emotional and social loneliness during young and middle adulthood. This study examined age-related differences in overall, emotional, and social loneliness and associated sociodemographic, social, health-related, and personality factors among adults in Germany.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We analysed nationally representative data from the German Family Demography Panel Study (FReDA), including 14,443 adults aged 18 to 51 years. Loneliness was assessed using the validated De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Short Scale, distinguishing overall, emotional, and social loneliness. Multivariable regression models examined associations with sociodemographic, social, health-related, and personality factors. Analyses were stratified by age and gender.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: High levels of loneliness were common, with 24.3% of participants reporting intense emotional loneliness, 29.6% intense overall loneliness, and 35.8% intense social loneliness. Overall loneliness remained relatively stable across age groups. In contrast, emotional loneliness was lower in older age groups, while social loneliness was higher. Social relationships showed some of the strongest associations with loneliness, particularly social loneliness: discussing personal matters within one's social network (β = -0.32, 95% CI -0.37 to -0.28) and having a partner (β = -0.21, 95% CI -0.26 to -0.16) were associated with lower social loneliness, while first-generation migration background was associated with higher social loneliness (β = 0.31, 95% CI 0.24 to 0.38). Mental health burdens were consistently associated with higher loneliness, especially emotional loneliness, with depressed mood showing the strongest association (β = 0.22, 95% CI 0.17 to 0.27). Among personality traits, agreeableness was associated with lower social loneliness (β = -0.19, 95% CI -0.22 to -0.17), whereas neuroticism was associated with higher emotional loneliness (β = 0.17, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.20). Gender differences were generally small, as were associations with physical health conditions.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Loneliness in young and middle adulthood is multidimensional, with emotional and social loneliness showing distinct age-related patterns and associated factors. Social relationships showed some of the strongest associations with lower loneliness, while mental health burdens and first-generation migration background were associated with higher loneliness. Public health strategies may benefit from considering different loneliness dimensions and psychosocial contexts.

items.title: Personalized stress detection from wearable physiological signals via Digital Twin-inspired subject embeddings and recurrent neural networks.
items.authors: Alharbi H.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The rising prevalence of psychological stress and its associated adverse health effects have created an urgent need for reliable and automated detection methods that move beyond traditional self-report tools. While wearable sensing systems offer a promising avenue for continuous monitoring, current systems often fail to account for individual physiological variability in stress responses. This leads to suboptimal performance when applied across diverse populations. To address this challenge, this paper presents a novel framework aimed at personalized stress detection in wearable sensing systems.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We introduce a DT-GRU framework centered on a trainable subject-embedding module that captures each individual's unique physiological traits, thereby forming a latent Digital Twin (DT). This personalized embedding is integrated with Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) features in the model's inference pathway, enabling the framework to utilize both temporal dynamics and subject identity for improved detection. The DT-GRU framework was rigorously evaluated on the WESAD dataset, incorporating various validation techniques, including subject-independent train-test splits and Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The results from the evaluation demonstrate significant improvements in classification accuracy and generalizability. The integration of the personalized subject-embedding was shown to enhance the model's performance across the diverse population represented in the dataset.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: These findings highlight the potential of the DT-GRU approach for deployment in real-world stress monitoring applications. By effectively accounting for individual physiological variability, the framework provides a more reliable and personalized method for automated stress detection, paving the way for more effective and scalable mental health monitoring solutions.

items.title: Health-related factors among seafarers based on the health ecology model: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Wu D, Chen S, Zheng H, Yu X, Yan B.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To explore the health status and its influencing factors among seafarers based on the Health Ecological Model, and to identify priority areas for health management.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A convenience sampling approach was used to administer a questionnaire survey to 106 seafarers from March to June 2026. The questionnaire was developed based on the Health Ecological Model and covers general information, health status, health-influencing factors, and health management needs. Multiple linear regression analysis was performed using SPSS 26.0.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The total health score was 29.65 ± 3.62 (theoretical range: 2-32). Policy environment ( β  = 0.602, p  < 0.001) and behavioral characteristics ( β  = 0.260, p  = 0.015) were independent influencing factors of the total health score, with an adjusted R2 of 0.574. Further analysis revealed that the policy environment had the greatest impact on physical health ( β  = 0.526, p  < 0.001), while the interpersonal network was selectively associated with mental health ( β  = 0.207, p  = 0.030). The top three health management needs were improving onboard dietary structure (87.7%), strengthening occupational health training (35.9%), and upgrading onboard medical facilities (31.1%).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The overall health status of seafarers was at a relatively good level, with policy environment and behavioral characteristics being the main influencing factors. Health management should prioritize improving health security policies and onboard dietary structure, while strengthening occupational health training.

items.title: 'Even if you are guilty, you're still a human being': the impact of stigma on dignity and quality of healthcare from the perspective of people detained in police custody in England.
items.authors: Addison M, Mulrine S, McKinnon I, Rees G.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The aim of this paper is to explore harms to health and dignity generated through stigma from the perspective of people detained in police custody, a neglected population in healthcare research. We adopt an original theoretical approach, bringing together a human rights lens to health, stigma, and the Inverse Care Law (ICL) to show how stigma contributes to the degradation of dignity and poor experiences of quality care within custody.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The study utilises qualitative semi-structured interviews with 41 people with experience of being detained in police custody, across two police constabulary locations (North and South England). Data were analysed thematically using NVivo qualitative software.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Detainees experienced stigma whilst in police custody because of identity characteristics, status, drug use, mental health, and frequent healthcare requests. Stigmatising and dehumanising interactions with detention officers (DO) and Healthcare Practitioners (HCPs) align with harms to health and wellbeing, and contributed to a degradation of dignity amongst detainees.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This novel research reveals that the impact of stigma in police custody settings materialise as harms to health and wellbeing, and poorer quality healthcare. We argue that stigma interactions in custody settings undermine a human rights approach to health specified in the AAAQ standards set out by the World Health Organisation, and also reproduce the inverse care law. As part of a wider recommended overhaul of police custody in England and Wales, we advise this should include urgent anti-stigma work in police custody settings to address health inequities across delivery and provision of good quality health care.

items.title: Implementing digital mental health tools in the public behavioral health systems: a multi-city/county evaluation of California's Help@Hand project.
items.authors: Bevens W, Stoeckl SE, Eikey E, Schneider M, Stadnick NA, Zheng K, Mukamel DB, Sorkin DH, Schueller SM.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) can expand access to mental health care, particularly in underserved regions. Despite this, real-world implementation is complex and few studies have investigated the factors that shape it. We provide insights from Help@Hand, a five-year implementation project deploying DMHIs within public systems across counties and cities (i.e. sites) in California. This study examined how these sites implemented DMHIs within their local systems and identified factors that facilitated or prevented success.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Data were collected from project leads at participating sites (N = 12) through four waves of surveys and two rounds of interviews. Surveys and interviews were informed by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) and were iteratively adapted across waves to capture implementation experiences at different points in the project. Interviews and surveys were analyzed using a sequential mixed-methods design. Reflexive thematic analysis and descriptive survey statistics were used to examine implementation strategies, challenges, and adaptations.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Integrating four surveys and two interviews, we identified seven themes whose prominence differed across project stages: (1) vendors supplemented internal expertise but offered limited customization and data access; (2) workforce challenges were common where all sites reported early labor shortages that resolved at later stages; (3) transitions to sustainment proved challenging as no sites obtained new funding at the final survey; (4) community outreach shifted toward targeted, multimodal approaches; (5) centralized project management aided contracting and coordination but introduced delays to approvals; (6) cross-site collaboration declined as the project progressed; (7) digital equity remained challenging despite greater outreach efforts reported by final project stages.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This study provides several insights into the implementation of DMHIs within public behavioral health systems: hybrid centralized-local governance models can support coordination but may add layers of decision-making; the same determinants may be differentially experienced across sites depending on their local context; sustainment can be difficult, even with planning, where funding is difficult to obtain. We also demonstrate that the CFIR has utility in structuring implementation evaluations across multiple sites and project stages. Future multi-site DMHI initiatives should pair centralized coordination with flexible local pathways, account for differential site capacity, resource sustainment from the outset, and use frameworks such as the CFIR to structure their implementation evaluation.

items.title: Phenomenology, Etiology, and Severity of Delirium Among Patients Referred to Consultation-liaison Psychiatry Services in a Tertiary Care Hospital: A Cross-sectional Study.
items.authors: Jha P, Arun Bhat P, Shrinivasa Bhat U.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Delirium is an acute neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by disturbances in attention, awareness, and cognition. It is highly prevalent among hospitalized patients but remains under-recognized, particularly in its hypoactive form. Consultation-liaison psychiatry (CLP) services are pivotal for early identification, yet detailed clinical profiles from Indian tertiary-care settings are sparse.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This hospital-based cross-sectional study enrolled 94 adult inpatients referred for acute confusional states between October 2022 and April 2024. We used the Delirium Rating Scale-Revised-98 (DRS-R-98), the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS), and the Delirium Etiology Checklist (DEC). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square tests, and one-way ANOVA. Statistical significance was set at p <.05.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The mean age was 59.29 ± 16.12 years; 81.9% were male. Severe impairment was most frequent in attention (52.1%), short-term memory (50.0%), and orientation (48.9%). Hyperactive delirium was predominant (81.9%). The cohort's mean total DRS-R-98 score was 21.94 ± 8.12. Increasing age showed a significant association with delirium subtype ( F = 5.68, p =.005), with mixed and hypoactive presentations occurring in older patients. Metabolic/endocrine disturbances (91.5%) and systemic infections (40.4%) were the leading etiological contributors.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Delirium in CLP referrals is characterized by marked cognitive impairment, predominance of hyperactive presentation, and multifactorial etiology. The over-representation of hyperactive cases likely reflects referral bias. Structured assessment tools and routine screening are essential for early detection, particularly of hypoactive delirium. Future multicenter prospective studies are warranted.

items.title: Insights on Designing the MINT (Micro-Interventions for Navigating Tension) Chatbot System for Stress Management: Collaborative Autoethnography.
items.authors: Bolpagni M, Piffer SA, Pozza M, Maminimini M, Gabrielli S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Digital microinterventions are increasingly used to support stress self-management in everyday life. While previous research has examined their feasibility, adherence, and preliminary effectiveness, much less is known about how these interventions are experienced over extended periods of real-world use.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study used collaborative autoethnography (CAE) to examine the everyday experience of living with MINT (Micro-Interventions for Navigating Tension), a Telegram-based chatbot for stress management. Our goal was not to evaluate clinical outcomes but to understand how scheduled microinterventions fit into everyday life, when they were ignored, and when people relied on other ways of coping instead, and to identify implications for the design of future digital mental health tools.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a 4-week CAE involving 5 digital mental health researchers, who used the MINT chatbot as both participants and researchers. The experience was documented through multiple qualitative and quantitative sources, including reflective diaries, ecological momentary assessments (EMAs), workshop discussions, and wearable data, and analyzed collaboratively using reflexive thematic analysis (RTA).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Six interconnected themes described how MINT was experienced in everyday life: (T1) the importance of timing and emotional receptivity, (T2) the need for reciprocity and relational continuity, (T3) the tendency to favor existing coping strategies over suggested exercises, (T4) the meaning of nonengagement during periods of high stress, (T5) the collapse of self-initiated use after reminders were removed, and (T6) how everyday experiences with consumer wearables and general-purpose large language models reshaped expectations of digital mental health systems.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Our findings show that CAE complements conventional evaluations of digital mental health interventions by revealing aspects of everyday use that are difficult to capture through feasibility studies, large-scale trials, or looking at usage data. Beyond the specific case of MINT, they suggest that future stress-management systems should better account for users' receptivity, provide greater continuity across interactions, build on existing coping strategies, and help users move from externally prompted engagement to autonomous self-management.

items.title: User Perceptions of a Large Language Model-Based Chatbot for Cognitive Reappraisal of Stress: Mixed Methods Feasibility Study.
items.authors: Bhattacharjee A, Suh J, Chandra M, Hernandez J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Cognitive reappraisal is a widely studied emotion regulation strategy that helps individuals reinterpret stressful situations in ways that reduce their emotional impact. Digital mental health (DMH) tools often struggle to support this process because scripted templates fail to adapt to the varied and incomplete ways users describe their stressors. Large language models (LLMs) offer opportunities to increase conversational flexibility while preserving structured intervention steps.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to examine the feasibility of an LLM-based single-session intervention (SSI) for stress reappraisal. We assessed whether the activity was associated with short-term improvements in stress-related outcomes, and explored the design tensions that arose during user interactions.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a feasibility study with 100 employees from a large US technology company. Participants completed a structured cognitive reappraisal session delivered by a GPT-4o-based chatbot within Qualtrics. Pre-post measures included situational stress intensity, stress mindset, perceived demand, and perceived resources (all 5-point scales). Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. To complement self-reports, we analyzed sentiment and stress trajectories across conversation tertiles using a Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach (RoBERTa; BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) sentiment classifier, a RoBERTa stress classifier, and an LLM-based stress rater. We also conducted a thematic analysis of participants' open-ended responses covering stress impact, perspective change, liked and disliked aspects, and improvement suggestions, alongside their conversation logs.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Significant reductions were observed in situational stress intensity (mean 0.29, SD 0.83, r _rb=0.54; P =.002) and significant improvements in stress mindset (mean 1.70, SD 4.37, r _rb=0.44; P =.002). Sentiment and stress classifiers showed consistent declines in negative sentiment and stress from conversation start to end (all omnibus Friedman tests P <.001). Thematic analysis of open-ended responses surfaced several patterns in how participants engaged with the activity: they valued the structured prompts for organizing their thoughts, described shifts in how they interpreted their stressors, used the interaction to identify concrete next steps, and experienced the chatbot as a nonjudgmental space for reflection. Reported design tensions included perceived scriptedness, variable preferences for conversation length, and mixed reactions to AI-driven empathy.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: An LLM-enhanced cognitive reappraisal activity showed promise to be delivered as a brief digital intervention and is associated with short-term improvements in situational stress and stress mindset. Participants appreciated the clarity and reflection supported by the structured sequence, while noting important design challenges in balancing structure with conversational naturalness and contextual depth. These findings highlight both the promise and the design constraints of integrating LLMs into DMH interventions.

abstract.text:
Cognitive reappraisal is a widely studied emotion regulation strategy that helps individuals reinterpret stressful situations in ways that reduce their emotional impact. Digital mental health (DMH) tools often struggle to support this process because scripted templates fail to adapt to the varied and incomplete ways users describe their stressors. Large language models (LLMs) offer opportunities to increase conversational flexibility while preserving structured intervention steps.

This study aimed to examine the feasibility of an LLM-based single-session intervention (SSI) for stress reappraisal. We assessed whether the activity was associated with short-term improvements in stress-related outcomes, and explored the design tensions that arose during user interactions.

We conducted a feasibility study with 100 employees from a large US technology company. Participants completed a structured cognitive reappraisal session delivered by a GPT-4o-based chatbot within Qualtrics. Pre-post measures included situational stress intensity, stress mindset, perceived demand, and perceived resources (all 5-point scales). Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. To complement self-reports, we analyzed sentiment and stress trajectories across conversation tertiles using a Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach (RoBERTa; BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) sentiment classifier, a RoBERTa stress classifier, and an LLM-based stress rater. We also conducted a thematic analysis of participants' open-ended responses covering stress impact, perspective change, liked and disliked aspects, and improvement suggestions, alongside their conversation logs.

Significant reductions were observed in situational stress intensity (mean 0.29, SD 0.83, r _rb=0.54; P =.002) and significant improvements in stress mindset (mean 1.70, SD 4.37, r _rb=0.44; P =.002). Sentiment and stress classifiers showed consistent declines in negative sentiment and stress from conversation start to end (all omnibus Friedman tests P <.001). Thematic analysis of open-ended responses surfaced several patterns in how participants engaged with the activity: they valued the structured prompts for organizing their thoughts, described shifts in how they interpreted their stressors, used the interaction to identify concrete next steps, and experienced the chatbot as a nonjudgmental space for reflection. Reported design tensions included perceived scriptedness, variable preferences for conversation length, and mixed reactions to AI-driven empathy.

An LLM-enhanced cognitive reappraisal activity showed promise to be delivered as a brief digital intervention and is associated with short-term improvements in situational stress and stress mindset. Participants appreciated the clarity and reflection supported by the structured sequence, while noting important design challenges in balancing structure with conversational naturalness and contextual depth. These findings highlight both the promise and the design constraints of integrating LLMs into DMH interventions.

summary.text: An LLM-enhanced cognitive reappraisal activity showed promise to be delivered as a brief digital intervention and is associated with short-term improvements in situational stress and stress mindset. Participants appreciated the clarity and reflection supported by the structured sequence, while noting important design challenges in balancing structure with conversational naturalness and contextual depth. These findings highlight both the promise and the design constraints of integrating LLMs into DMH interventions.

items.title: An interpretable multimodal deep learning model for physiological stress detection.
items.authors: Tibermacine A, Tibermacine IE, Mancer M, Rabehi A, Guettala W, Habib M.

sections.text: Stress is a major contributor to physical and mental health disorders, underscoring the need for reliable and interpretable detection systems. We present an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework that integrates electrocardiogram (ECG), electrodermal activity (EDA), and respiration signals using modality-specific neural architectures complemented by feature-based classical models. To ensure robustness and generalizability, the framework was evaluated under both subject-independent and subject-dependent protocols. Results show that multimodal fusion consistently outperformed single modalities, achieving 94.8% accuracy, 93.9% F1-score, and 0.97 AUC under subject-independent validation, compared with 86-91% accuracy for individual signals. In subject-dependent experiments, performance reached 97.2% accuracy and 96.8% F1-score. Comparative analysis with recent state-of-the-art methods demonstrated the competitiveness of our approach, while ablation studies confirmed the contribution of each modality and fusion strategy. Statistical significance testing with (p < 0.05) further validated the reliability of these gains. Importantly, interpretability analyses using Grad-CAM and attention visualization provided physiological insights, revealing that the model emphasizes clinically meaningful regions such as ECG R-peaks and phasic EDA fluctuations. By uniting high performance, robustness, and interpretability, this work advances stress detection research and offers a physiologically grounded framework for continuous mental health monitoring.

items.title: The need for supportive policies: connecting individual placement and support to the domains of employment and mental health care.
items.authors: van Weeghel J, Fioritti A, Jaeckel D, Johnston G, Mazzetti G, Ahola M, Bejerholm U, Bergmans C, Debroas F, de Winter L, Einarsdottir SE, Guglielmi D, Jónasson H, Kárníková A, Koatz D, Kropeit J, Lunder Arvesen AL, Manchisi D, Markerink J, Nan Lium K, Sipilä N, Twomey U, Van Audenhove C.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Individual placement and support (IPS) is an effective vocational rehabilitation programme for people with mental illness. This article analyses national policies that directly promote IPS and broader employment-related policies on mental health in 13 European countries.

sections.heading: Analysis
sections.text: IPS alone cannot address the broader workplace and policy conditions that influence sustainable employment. Therefore, creating mentally healthy working conditions also requires action by employers, healthcare systems, and policymakers.

sections.heading: Policy options
sections.text: Recurring barriers and facilitators were identified across countries, alongside variation in governance and implementation contexts. IPS services often operate in isolation, with limited access to consistent training, data, and cross-sector coordination. A national infrastructure for IPS is therefore needed to offer implementation support, intersectoral collaboration should be strengthened and employers need to be supported to advance equity, diversity and inclusion. IPS practice will benefit from policies addressing poor mental health conditions in the workplace, and policies endorsing a recovery-oriented mental healthcare system.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: IPS can build a solid bridge between mental healthcare and employment when integrated into recovery-oriented services and supported by policies that promote inclusive, mentally healthy workplaces.

items.title: Measurement properties of the EQ-5D-5L and SF-6D in measuring the health-related quality of life of non-small cell lung cancer patients on active treatments in China.
items.authors: Wang J, Suo Y, Wang Y, Li Y, Wang L, Guan X, Guo Y, Yang M, Wang H, Zhu H, Liang W, Song N, Xu Y, Wang J, Tang L, Ye Z, Xie F, Li H, Jin X.
items.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death globally, including China, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounting for 85% of cases. Novel NSCLC drugs need cost-utility analysis (CUA) for Chinese reimbursement. CUA relies on health utility values, but the only measures with value sets for Chinese populations, i.e., EQ-5D-5L and SF-6D, lack NSCLC-specific reliability and validity comparison evidence. This study examined their measurement properties in Chinese patients with NSCLC.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional survey was conducted across 18 provincial-level jurisdictions in China (2022.10-2024.03) with 947 patients from 20 hospitals. EQ-5D-5L, SF-6D, and QLQ-C30 were administered to patients, and a total of 886 patients with complete responses to all three aforementioned measures were included in the analysis of this study. Measurement properties were evaluated via ceiling/floor effects, convergent validity (with QLQ-C30), known-groups validity (gender, age, cancer stage, surgery, brain metastasis, bone metastasis, and COVID-19 infection history), and Shannon (H') and evenness (J') indices.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among the analysis sample (n = 886), participants were 36.5% female with a mean age of 61.5 years and a mean disease duration of 1.8 years; 64.1% had stage IV disease. Ceiling effects for the EQ-5D-5L and SF-6D were 26.07% and 3.50%, respectively. Both tools showed moderate-to-strong correlations with relevant QLQ-C30 dimensions (|rho| = 0.58-0.84, all p < 0.001). For known-groups validity, small-to-medium effect sizes were found for subgroups of age, cancer stage, operation, and bone metastasis for EQ-5D-5L; and cancer stage, operation, bone metastasis, and COVID-19 infection history for SF-6D. Regarding informativity, H'/J' ranged from 1.061/0.457 for "Self-care" to 1.737/0.748 for "Pain/discomfort" for EQ-5D-5L, and 1.925/0.829 for "mental health" to 2.223/0.957 for "social functioning" for SF-6D.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Both the EQ-5D-5L and SF-6D have robust measurement properties for assessing health status in Chinese NSCLC patients.

items.title: State and Local Policymakers' Engagement with Neuroscience to Improve Health Policy in the United States.
items.authors: Levine AS, Mathews DJH, Boyd JL.

sections.text: Neuroscience is useful for making progress on public health challenges such as mental health, aging, violence, and addiction. State and local policymakers have substantial authority over these issues but do not always have access to the research and counsel they want. To inform initiatives that could bridge the gap, high-quality information on policymakers' existing and desired engagement is needed. We conducted four nationally representative surveys of local elected policymakers, local public sector staff, state legislators, and state public sector staff to gather this information. Across the four samples, 13.8-28.6% reported recently interacting with a neuroscientist, while 50.3-73.6% reported unmet desire to do so. Prior exposure to disseminated neuroscience information varied, from 19.1 to 68.0% across the samples. Unmet desire for neuroscience-related policy briefs (50.5-76.8%) and news articles (52.7-68.9%) were among the most common for all policymakers. Unmet desire crossed party lines, though with some partisan differences. These findings suggest several avenues to increase evidence-informed health policymaking.

items.title: Sleep disturbance is associated with reduced DTI-ALPS index and altered functional-network efficiency in internet gaming disorder.
items.authors: Ma L, Mei B, Zhang M, Li W, Wang X, Tian J, Zhang H, Lang Y, Lv Q, Wei Y, Han S, Zhang Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Sleep disturbance is common in internet gaming disorder (IGD), but its possible involvement in the pathophysiology of IGD remains unclear. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the glymphatic system-related function in IGD patients and to establish the associations among glymphatic system, human brain network, and clinical features.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This study recruited 66 IGD patients and 35 healthy controls (HC), who underwent magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanning and clinical assessment. The glymphatic system-related diffusivity and network efficiency were calculated based on diffusion images along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) method and resting-state functional MRI, respectively. Differences between groups, neural/clinical correlations, and mediation analyses were further explored.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Compared with HC, IGD patients showed a significantly lower ALPS index and global network efficiency. The partial correlation analysis showed that the ALPS index in IGD patients was associated with PSQI, HAMA, and HAMD scores. Moreover, the ALPS index partially mediated the association between global brain efficiency and sleep quality in exploratory cross-sectional mediation analysis.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The current study revealed abnormalities of ALPS index and network efficiency in IGD patients and suggested that the cross-sectional associations among global brain efficiency, sleep quality, and ALPS index were consistent with an indirect pathway, which may reveal the neuropathological mechanisms of IGD.

items.title: From need satisfaction to academic achievement: pathways through wellbeing and engagement among university students across different Italian institutions.
items.authors: Florean I, Gemignani M, Colella GM, Verrastro V, Liga F, Inguglia C, Saputo E, Grassini S, Venuti P, Penolazzi B, D'Urso G, Craig F.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: University students face personal and academic demands that may challenge their adaptive functioning. Although intrinsic goals, need satisfaction, wellbeing, and academic engagement have been distinctively linked to academic achievement, an integrated model specifying how these constructs are structurally related and associated with students' academic outcomes is lacking. The present study addresses this gap by testing models grounded in Self-Determination Theory and previous evidence.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Participants were 2891 university students ( M _ age = 23.22 years, SD _ age = 5.25 years; 74.75% women) recruited across multiple Italian universities. The online survey comprised different measures, including socio-demographic items, the Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction and Frustration Scale, the Aspiration Index, the SInAPSi Academic Engagement Scale, and the Mental Health Continuum-Short Form. Structural equation modeling was used to test two alternative model specifications. Starting from a more general model, progressively more parsimonious models were tested by constraining selected direct effects. The final model was selected based on comparative fit, overall model fit, parsimony, and theoretical coherence.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The retained model specified wellbeing as antecedent to academic engagement. Within this model, basic psychological need satisfaction showed indirect links to academic achievement through wellbeing and academic engagement, while intrinsic goals were related to achievement only through academic engagement. Academic engagement emerged as the most proximal predictor of achievement, mediating the pathways from need satisfaction, intrinsic goals, and wellbeing.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings provide an integrated account of how satisfaction of basic psychological needs, intrinsic motivations, wellbeing, and academic engagement relate to academic achievement in university students. Our evidence supports a model in which psychological need satisfaction represents a relevant condition associated with wellbeing, intrinsic goals contribute more specifically to academic engagement, and academic engagement acts as the proximal mechanism linking these factors with academic achievement. Beyond advancing theoretical understanding, our results may inform preventive programs and interventions nurturing students' wellbeing while also promoting their academic performance.

items.title: What is gratitude research missing? Bridging the gap between conceptualization, measurement, and intervention.
items.authors: Del Rosario-Gilabert D, Regalado-Reyes M, Vila-Brunet N.

sections.text: Does contemporary gratitude research investigate the full phenomenon described by current gratitude theories? Gratitude has become a prominent construct in positive psychology, with research linking it to well-being, resilience, prosociality, and mental health. As theoretical perspectives have expanded, however, empirical approaches appear not to have broadened to the same extent. This purposive Mini review examines gratitude research across conceptualization, measurement, intervention, physiology, and neuroscience. Contemporary theories and measures increasingly represent gratitude as a multidimensional phenomenon encompassing interpersonal, existential, contemplative, embodied, and ecological dimensions. By contrast, dominant and influential intervention paradigms continue to emphasize reflection on benefits and benefactors, while much of the neuroscience literature reviewed here operationalizes gratitude through interpersonal, appraisal-based, and reciprocity-related scenarios. These differences suggest a conceptual-operational mismatch: relatively broad understandings of gratitude are often investigated through more narrowly focused empirical approaches. Consequently, existing findings may illuminate interpersonal and benefit-focused gratitude more fully than broader forms of grateful experience. We conclude by proposing directions for developing ecologically valid, embodied, and relational methodologies capable of investigating a wider range of gratitude experiences.
